definition_zh: 断层；过错；缺点；故障；责任
definition_en: a break in rock where one side has moved; also a mistake, a defect or responsibility for something wrong
core_image: 一层层岩体被拉开，两侧错位，形成一条可见的裂缝，裂缝两边的高度不再对齐
scene: 多年积累的应力终于释放，岩层沿一条裂缝突然错动。Movement along a fault released the strain that had built up for years.
sceneCN: 这里 fault 指「断层」（第 1 个义项：岩层两侧发生相对位移的破裂面）；句意为沿断层的运动释放了多年积累的应变。

挑出……的毛病；使产生断层

senses.title: A break in rock
senses.titleCN: 断层：岩层破裂并发生位移
senses.definition: a break in rock along which one side has moved relative to the other
senses.definitionCN: 岩层中的破裂面，其一侧相对另一侧发生了移动
senses.example: Movement along a fault released the strain that had built up for years.
senses.exampleCN: 沿断层的运动释放了多年积累的应变。
senses.why: The geological sense comes from mining: a fault is where a seam of ore fails or is cut off.
senses.whyCN: 地质义来自采矿：断层就是矿层「断掉」或被截断的地方。

senses.title: A mistake or wrongdoing
senses.definition: a mistake or wrongful act
senses.definitionCN: 错误或不当的行为
senses.example: The delay was my fault, not yours.
senses.exampleCN: 延误是我的过错，不是你的。
senses.why: The oldest English sense is 'a failing or defect', which then attaches to the person who caused it.
senses.whyCN: 英语最早的义项是「缺失或缺陷」，后来附到造成缺陷的人身上。

senses.title: A defect in character
senses.titleCN: 缺点：性格或事物上的缺陷
senses.definition: a weakness or flaw in a person's character or in a thing
senses.definitionCN: 人的性格或事物上的弱点、缺陷
senses.example: Generosity is his one fault as a negotiator.
senses.exampleCN: 过于大方是他作为谈判者的唯一缺点。
senses.why: A fault is literally a break or gap, so an imperfect character is described as having a break in it.
senses.whyCN: fault 字面就是断裂或缺口，所以有缺陷的性格被描述为身上有一处断口。

senses.title: A technical fault
senses.titleCN: 故障：设备或系统的失灵
senses.definition: a failure in a machine, system or process
senses.definitionCN: 机器、系统或过程中的失灵
senses.example: A fault in the wiring cut the power.
senses.exampleCN: 线路故障切断了电力。
senses.why: A machine fails where a connection breaks, so the mining sense of a break survives in engineering.
senses.whyCN: 机器在连接断开处失灵，所以采矿中「断裂」的意思在工程里保留下来。

senses.title: Responsibility for something wrong
senses.definition: responsibility for a mistake or for something bad that happened
senses.definitionCN: 对错误或不幸事件应负的责任
senses.example: The driver was at fault in the accident.
senses.exampleCN: 司机在这起事故中负有责任。
senses.why: If a fault is a defect, being at fault means the defect is located in you.
senses.whyCN: 如果 fault 是缺陷，那么 at fault 就意味着缺陷落在你身上。

senses.title: The fault plane
senses.titleCN: 断层面：断层两侧的接触面
senses.definition: the surface along which the two sides of a fault have slipped
senses.definitionCN: 断层两侧沿之滑动的面
senses.example: The fault plane dips steeply to the east.
senses.exampleCN: 断层面向东陡倾。
senses.why: Every fault has a surface of contact, so the noun extends to the geometry of that surface.
senses.whyCN: 每条断层都有一个接触面，因此这个名词也指该面的几何形态。

senses.title: A tennis service fault
senses.definition: in tennis, a serve that misses the legal area
senses.definitionCN: 网球中未落入合法区域的发球
senses.example: She served a fault and had to try again.
senses.exampleCN: 她发球失误，只好重发。
senses.why: The serve fails to land where it should, so the general 'failure' sense survives in sport.
senses.whyCN: 发球没有落到应在的位置，所以「失败」这一通用义在体育中保留下来。

senses.title: To find fault
senses.definition: to criticise small defects in someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 对人或事物的小缺陷加以批评
senses.example: He finds fault with every plan we propose.
senses.exampleCN: 他挑我们提出的每一个方案的毛病。
senses.why: Finding fault is literally locating the defect, and the phrase shifted from diagnosis to complaint.
senses.whyCN: find fault 字面就是找出缺陷，这个短语从「诊断」转为「抱怨」。

intro.en: Fault comes from Latin fallere 'to deceive, fail' through Old French. The sense of a rock break grew out of mining language, where a seam 'fails'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: fault 经古法语来自拉丁语 fallere「欺骗、失败」。岩石破裂义从采矿用语发展而来，那里矿层会「断掉」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Fallere meant 'to deceive, disappoint, fail'; its past participle falsus gave false, and its noun sense of failure underlies fault.
items.cn: fallere 意为「欺骗、令人失望、失败」；其过去分词 falsus 产生 false，而「失败」的名词义构成 fault 的基础。

items.en: Old French faute meant 'a lack, a defect, a mistake'; the form lost the l and gained the sense of blame.
items.cn: 古法语 faute 意为「缺失、缺陷、错误」；这个词形丢了 l，并获得「责备」的意思。

items.en: Middle English restored an l under Latin influence, giving fault, and used it for defects of body, character and action.
items.cn: 中古英语在拉丁语影响下补回了 l，写成 fault，并用它指身体、性格与行为上的缺陷。

items.en: Miners called a break that cut off a seam a fault, and later writers used the word for shortfalls and blame.
items.cn: 矿工把截断矿层的断裂称为 fault，地质学家据此把这个词用于任何发生位移的岩石破裂。

items.en: Engineering added electrical and mechanical faults, sport added the tennis fault, and the phrase at fault fixed the sense of blame.
items.cn: 工程领域增加了电气与机械故障义，体育增加了网球发球失误义，短语 at fault 则固定了「担责」义。

items.en: The step from Latin fallere to Old French faute is generally accepted, but the exact medieval transmission is reconstructed rather than directly documented.
items.cn: 从拉丁语 fallere 到古法语 faute 这一步一般认为成立，但中古时期的具体传播路径是重构的，而非有直接文献记录。

note.en: Group one holds words that look or sound close to fault; group two holds words for defects and blame that differ in scope.
note.cn: 第一组是形音接近 fault 的词；第二组是表示缺陷与责任但范围不同的词。

entries.definition: the adjective meaning 'defective'; fault is the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 表示「有缺陷的」形容词；fault 是名词。

entries.definition: an arched ceiling or a leap; it begins with /v/, not /f/.
entries.definitionCN: 拱顶，或跳跃；开头是 /v/ 而不是 /f/。

entries.definition: false or imitation, as in faux fur; it is a French borrowing without the final -lt.
entries.definitionCN: 假的、仿制的，如人造毛；它是法语借词，结尾没有 -lt。

entries.definition: failure to do something required, or an automatic setting; the de- prefix adds 'away from'.
entries.definitionCN: 未履行应做之事，或自动默认设置；前缀 de- 增添了「离开」的意思。

entries.definition: an imperfection in a product or a body; it stresses the missing quality rather than blame.
entries.definitionCN: 产品或身体上的不完美；它强调缺失的质量，而不是责备。

entries.definition: a weakness that may be hidden and may ruin something; it is often subtler than a fault.
entries.definitionCN: 可能隐蔽并毁掉某物的弱点；通常比 fault 更细微。

entries.definition: a wrong action or wrong result; it may be accidental and carries less blame than fault.
entries.definitionCN: 错误的行为或结果；可能是无意的，责备意味比 fault 轻。

entries.definition: responsibility for something bad; fault is the defect, blame is the judgement placed on a person.
entries.definitionCN: 对坏事的责任；fault 是缺陷，blame 是加在某人身上的评判。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the word's own history links rock breaks, defects and blame, so the senses can be held together by one image.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：这个词自身的历史把岩石破裂、缺陷与责备连在一起，因此各义项可用一个形象串起。

normal.en: A fault is a break: rock breaks, a machine breaks, a character has a break, and blame marks where the break is.
normal.cn: fault 就是断口：岩石断开、机器断开、性格有断口，而责备标明断口在哪里。

normal.en: Miners met a fault where a seam stopped, which is how the geological sense was born.
normal.cn: 矿工在矿层中断处遇到 fault，地质义就是这样诞生的。

normal.en: At fault means the defect is located in you, so responsibility follows the image.
normal.cn: at fault 表示缺陷落在你身上，责任便顺着这个形象而来。

normal.en: A tennis fault is a serve that fails to land in the right box, a small failure of the same kind.
normal.cn: 网球 fault 是发球没有落进正确区域，是同一类的小失败。

normal.en: Fault line and fault plane are both built from the geological sense, so learn them as a set.
normal.cn: fault line 与 fault plane 都出自地质义，可以成组记忆。

abstract.en: Abstractly, fault is a discontinuity: something that should be continuous is broken, whether rock, wire or character.
abstract.cn: 抽象地看，fault 是一种不连续：本应连续的东西断了，无论是岩石、电线还是性格。

abstract.en: The word moves easily between the physical and the moral because both are read as breaks in a whole.
abstract.cn: 这个词在物理与道德之间移动自如，因为两者都被读作整体上的断口。

abstract.en: Symbol: two blocks offset along a diagonal seam, with a small arrow showing the slip.
abstract.cn: 符号：两块岩体沿一条斜缝错开，旁边一个小箭头表示滑动方向。

examples.en: The San Andreas Fault is a famous example of a transform fault.
examples.cn: 圣安德烈斯断层是一条著名的转换断层。

examples.en: The failure was not entirely his fault.
examples.cn: 这次失败并不完全是他的过错。

examples.en: Engineers traced the fault to a loose connector.
examples.cn: 工程师把故障追查到一处松动的接头。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「缝特」—— 岩层裂开一条特别的缝，两边错位 → fault 断层、过错

root: 源自拉丁语 fallere（欺骗、失败），经古法语 faute 进入英语，核心含义是「缺失、断口」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of fault. The core is a break or gap, which becomes a rock break, a defect, a machine failure or a blame.
sensesIntro.cn: fault 的八个义项。核心是断口或缺口，由此变成岩石破裂、缺陷、机器故障或责备。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a break where two sides no longer line up.
core.cn: 核心意象：一处断口，两侧不再对齐。

branches.en: ROCK: a break with displacement, and the surface along which it slips.
branches.cn: 岩石：发生位移的破裂，以及沿之滑动的面。

branches.en: CHARACTER DEFECT: a weakness of character.
branches.cn: 性格缺陷：性格上的弱点。

branches.en: TENNIS FAULT: a serve misses the legal target.
branches.cn: 网球失误：发球未落入合法区域。

branches.en: BLAME: locating the defect in a person, and complaining about small defects.
branches.cn: 责备：把缺陷定位到某人身上，或对小缺陷加以抱怨。

branches.en: SMALL FAILURES: a wrong act and a machine glitch are both a small break in an expected order.
branches.cn: 小失败：做错一件事与机器出一次故障，都是应有秩序中的一个小断口。

intro.en: Fault has a small but productive family: two adjectives, a process noun and the prefixed word default.
intro.cn: fault 有一个小而能产的词族：两个形容词、一个过程名词，以及带前缀的 default。

latinIntro.en: The Latin source is fallere 'to deceive, fail' and its participle falsus; Old French faute supplies the noun, and de- plus fallere gives default.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语来源是 fallere「欺骗、失败」及其分词 falsus；古法语 faute 提供名词，de- 加 fallere 构成 default。

items.example: The root also gives false and falsify.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根也产生 false 与 falsify。

items.meaning: a missing quality or a wrong act
items.meaningCN: 缺失的品质或错误的行为
items.example: The French noun passed into English as fault.
items.exampleCN: 这个法语名词进入英语成为 fault。

items.meaningCN: 有缺陷的（-y 构成形容词）
items.example: The faulty cable caused the outage.
items.exampleCN: 有故障的电缆造成了停电。

items.meaningCN: 没有缺陷的（-less 表示无）

items.meaning: the process of breaking and slipping in rock
items.meaningCN: 岩石破裂并滑动的过程

items.meaning: failure to act, or the standard setting
items.example: The system returned to its default.
The fault plane dips to the north.

items.meaning: a belt of broken rock around a fault
items.meaningCN: 断层周围破碎岩石构成的带
items.example: The fault zone is several kilometres wide.
items.exampleCN: 这条断层带宽达数公里。

items.meaning: the habit of criticising small defects
items.example: Constant fault-finding wore the team down.
items.exampleCN: 不断的挑剔使团队疲惫。

latinEntries.structure: falsus (perfect passive participle used as adjective)

definition_zh: 最喜爱的；特别受喜爱的；特别受喜爱的人（物）；宠儿；热门选手
definition_en: liked or preferred above all others, or the person or thing that is liked best
core_image: 一排同类东西里有一个被圈了出来，每次伸手都先拿它
scene: 冰淇淋车一到，孩子们围上去点各自钟情的口味。Vanilla is my favourite flavour, so I always choose it first.
sceneCN: 这里 favourite 是形容词，指「最喜爱的」，对应第 1 个义项；句意为香草是我最喜欢的口味。

pos.zh: 最喜爱的；特别受喜爱的
特别受喜爱的人（物）；宠儿；夺标热门

derivatives.zh: 偏袒；偏爱（favourite 的美式词根加 -ism 名词后缀，指不公地偏爱某人）
偏袒；偏爱（英式拼写，义同 favoritism）
恩惠；赞成；支持（favourite 的词根，拉丁语 favor「好感」）
有利的；赞同的（favor 加形容词后缀 -able，指条件有利或态度赞成）

senses.title: Liked above all others
senses.definition: preferred to all others of the same kind
senses.definitionCN: 在同类的所有对象中被排在最前面
senses.example: Blue is my favourite colour.
senses.exampleCN: 蓝色是我最喜欢的颜色。
senses.why: The core image is a hand that always reaches for the same one, so the word names the top pick.
senses.whyCN: 核心画面是一只手每次都拿同一个东西，所以这个词命名的是首选。

senses.title: A person or thing liked best
senses.definition: the person or thing that someone likes more than any other
senses.definitionCN: 某人胜过其他一切而最喜欢的人或物
senses.example: She quickly became the teacher's favourite.
senses.exampleCN: 她很快成了老师最喜欢的学生。
senses.why: The adjective settles into a noun: the top pick itself gets a name.
senses.whyCN: 形容词落定为名词：首选之物本身有了称呼。

senses.title: The expected winner
senses.definition: a competitor thought most likely to win a race or contest
senses.definitionCN: 被认为最有可能在比赛或竞争中获胜的选手
senses.example: She is the favourite to win the final.
senses.exampleCN: 她是决赛的夺冠热门。
senses.why: Being everyone's choice before a contest starts makes you the pick of the crowd.
senses.whyCN: 开赛前就被大家看好，你便成了众人心里的首选。

senses.title: Frequented or specially treated
senses.definition: visited often, or treated with special kindness
senses.definitionCN: 经常光顾的，或受到格外优待的
senses.example: They met at their favourite cafe.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在常去的那家咖啡馆见面。
senses.why: Places and people you return to again and again become your chosen ones.
senses.whyCN: 你一再回去的地方、一再善待的人，就成了你的偏爱。

intro.en: Favourite runs back to Latin favor 'good will, partiality', carried into English through Old French and shaped into an adjective-noun pair.
intro.cn: favourite 可回溯到拉丁语 favor「好感、偏袒」，经古法语进入英语，构成形容词与名词一对。

items.en: Favor meant 'good will, approval, partiality', from favere 'to show kindness'.
items.cn: favor 意为「好感、赞成、偏袒」，出自 favere「表示善意」。

items.en: Old French favor kept the sense of goodwill and support.
items.cn: 古法语 favor 保留了好感与支持的意思。

items.en: Middle English borrowed favor, then formed favourite as 'one who is favored'.
items.cn: 中古英语借入 favor，随后构成 favourite，意为「受宠之人」。

items.en: The word settled into the adjective-noun pair, and American spelling shortened it to favorite.
items.cn: 现代英语把它固定为形容词与名词一对，美式拼写简化为 favorite。

items.en: In everyday speech favourite now extends from books and food to public figures and race contenders.
items.cn: 在日常口语里，favourite 如今从书籍、食物扩展到公众人物与比赛选手。

note.en: Look-alikes share the favour root or a close shape; near-meaning words name preference and winners.
note.cn: 形近组共享 favour 词根或相近拼写；近义组表达偏爱与人选。

entries.definition: the same word spelled the American way
kindness or support shown to someone
entries.definitionCN: 对某人表现出的好意或支持；与 favourite 同根

entries.definition: the taste of food; only one letter apart but not related in meaning
entries.definitionCN: 食物的味道；拼写只差一个字母，但意义无关

entries.definition: chosen over other possibilities
entries.definitionCN: 被优先选择的；更受偏好的

entries.definition: dearly loved, often with warmth
a person especially liked or cherished
entries.definitionCN: 特别受宠爱的人；心肝宝贝

normalIntro.en: Five handles built from the favour root and everyday use.
normalIntro.cn: 五个基于 favour 词根与日常用法的记忆抓手。

normal.en: favourite contains favour: the thing you favour is your favourite.
normal.cn: favourite 里有 favour：你偏爱（favor）的东西就是你的最爱。

normal.en: British spelling keeps u, American spelling drops it: favourite / favorite.
normal.cn: 英式拼写保留 u，美式拼写删去：favourite / favorite。

normal.en: The teacher's favourite is the one called on with a smile.
normal.cn: 老师的宠儿，就是那个总被笑着点名的人。

normal.en: In racing the favourite is the horse everyone bets on first.
normal.cn: 赛马场上的热门，是大家最先押注的那匹马。

normal.en: The root favour itself means goodwill, so a favourite is a goodwill magnet.
normal.cn: 词根 favour 本义是好意，最受喜爱者就是好意的磁铁。

abstract.en: Imagine your shelf: everything else gathers dust, one item is worn smooth by your hands.
abstract.cn: 想象你的书架：其他都积了灰，唯独一件被你的手磨得光滑。

abstract.en: Preference is a spotlight that keeps returning to one face on the stage.
abstract.cn: 偏爱是一盏反复照向舞台上同一张脸的追光灯。

abstract.en: Being the favourite feels like gravity: attention falls toward you.
abstract.cn: 成为宠儿像引力一样：注意力总朝你落下来。

examples.en: Chocolate cake is my favourite dessert.
examples.cn: 巧克力蛋糕是我最喜欢的甜点。

examples.en: She is the favourite to win this year's singing contest.
examples.cn: 她是今年歌唱比赛的夺冠热门。

examples.en: The band played all their favourites at the concert.
examples.cn: 乐队在演唱会上演奏了他们所有的成名曲。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「肥窝里特」—— 最心爱的东西总被放在肥沃的窝里特别优待 → favourite 最喜爱的、宠儿

root: 源自拉丁语 favor（好感、偏袒），经古法语 favor 与「受宠者」构词进入英语；核心是「被给予好感的人或物」。

sensesIntro.en: From the top pick as an adjective to the beloved one, the expected winner and the habitual choice.
sensesIntro.cn: 从形容词上的「首选」，到心爱之物、夺标热门与常去常选的对象。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one item circled on a shelf of equals.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排同类中被圈出的那一个。

branches.en: TOP PICK: liked above all others.
THE BELOVED: the person or thing itself.
THE WINNER: expected to take the prize.
branches.cn: 热门：被认为会赢的选手。

branches.en: THE HABITUAL: the place or thing you keep returning to.
branches.cn: 常选：你一再回去的对象。

branches.en: PUBLIC CHOICE: crowd support turns a pick into a favourite.
branches.cn: 大众之选：众人的支持把首选变成热门。

intro.en: The favour family is wide: nouns, verbs and adjectives all grow from one Latin root.
intro.cn: favor 词族很广：名词、动词、形容词都出自同一个拉丁词根。

latinIntro.en: Latin favor 'good will' from favere 'to be favourable' supplies the whole family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 favor「好感」（出自 favere「示好」）供给整个词族。

items.example: Favoritism in grading upset the class.

items.meaning: taste; not from the favour root
items.meaningCN: 味道；与 favor 词根无关

items.example: The clown is a crowd favourite.

items.exampleCN: 他们演奏了那首老牌最爱。

latinEntries.meaning: I support, I am kind to

definition_zh: 害怕；恐惧；担忧；敬畏；害怕做某事
definition_en: an unpleasant feeling caused by the belief that something dangerous or painful might happen, or the act of being afraid
core_image: 黑暗里一步不敢挪动的身体，心跳加速，眼睛盯着可能出现的危险
scene: 停电的楼道里脚步声由远及近，孩子紧紧抓住门框。She could not move for fear of waking the dog.
sceneCN: 这里 fear 是名词，指「恐惧」这一情绪，对应第 1 个义项；句意为她一动不动，生怕惊醒狗。

derivatives.zh: 可怕的；害怕的（fear 加形容词后缀 -ful，指充满恐惧或令人恐惧）
无畏的；不怕的（fear 加 -less，指没有恐惧）
害怕地；非常地（fearful 加副词后缀 -ly）
无畏地（fearless 加副词后缀 -ly）

senses.title: The feeling of being afraid
senses.definition: an unpleasant emotion caused by the belief that someone or something is dangerous
senses.definitionCN: 因相信某人某物有危险而产生的不快情绪
senses.example: He has a fear of spiders.
senses.exampleCN: 他害怕蜘蛛。
senses.why: The body reacts before thinking, so the word first names the raw feeling itself.
senses.whyCN: 身体先于思考起反应，所以这个词首先指那种原始情绪。

senses.title: A worry about something specific
senses.definition: a worry that something bad may happen
senses.definitionCN: 对坏事可能发生的担忧
senses.example: Her biggest fear is failing the exam.
senses.exampleCN: 她最大的顾虑是考试不及格。
senses.why: When the danger is distant and imagined, the feeling softens into a worry.
senses.whyCN: 当危险遥远而只是想象时，这种感觉便弱化为担忧。

senses.title: To be afraid of something
senses.definition: to feel afraid of a person, thing or situation
senses.definitionCN: 对某人、某物或某种情况感到害怕
senses.example: Do not fear the dark; fear what hides in it.
senses.exampleCN: 不要怕黑，要怕藏在黑暗里的东西。
senses.why: The noun turns into a verb: the feeling itself becomes the act of feeling it.
senses.whyCN: 名词转为动词：情绪本身变成「感到这种情绪」这一动作。

senses.title: To expect something bad
senses.definition: to think that something bad has happened or will happen
senses.definitionCN: 认为坏事已经或将要发生
senses.example: I fear we are too late.
senses.exampleCN: 恐怕我们已经太迟了。
senses.why: Expecting the worst is fear pointed at the future, so the verb shifts to prediction.
senses.whyCN: 预期最坏的事就是指向未来的恐惧，于是动词偏向「料想」。

senses.title: Respect mixed with awe
senses.definition: respect for someone powerful, mixed with dread
senses.definitionCN: 对强者的敬重，其中夹杂畏惧
senses.example: They feared the old master's judgment.
senses.exampleCN: 他们敬畏老匠人的评判。
senses.why: Power that can hurt you earns both respect and dread, so fear stretches to cover awe.
senses.whyCN: 能伤害你的力量同时赢得敬重与畏惧，于是 fear 扩展到「敬畏」。

intro.en: Fear is a native Germanic word, grown from an Old English noun for sudden danger, and it has carried both emotion and expectation for a thousand years.
intro.cn: fear 是日耳曼本族词，由古英语表「突然危险」的名词发展而来，千年来一直兼指情绪与预料。

items.en: A reconstructed Germanic root feraz meant 'danger' or 'that which attacks'; cousins appear in German Gefahr.
items.cn: 一般认为，重构的日耳曼词根 feraz 意为「危险」或「来袭之物」；德语 Gefahr 是同族词。

items.en: Old English fer meant 'sudden danger or calamity', and the verb form grew beside it.
items.cn: 古英语 fer 意为「突发的危险或灾祸」，动词形式也随之生长。

items.en: Middle English fere covered both the emotion and the expected harm, as in for fear of.
items.cn: 中古英语 fere 兼指情绪与预期的祸害，如 for fear of（以免）。

items.en: Spelling settled as fear, and the word now leads a large family: fearful, fearless, fearfully.
items.cn: 现代英语拼写定为 fear，并形成大家族：fearful、fearless、fearfully。

items.en: Psychology and daily speech keep fear as the baseline word for all anxiety-like feelings.
items.cn: 心理学与日常语言都把 fear 当作一切类焦虑情绪的基础词。

note.en: Look-alikes share the shape fea-; near-meaning words occupy the wider field of dread and worry.
note.cn: 形近组共享 fea- 字形；近义组占据恐惧与担忧这一更大的义场。

entries.definition: to receive sound with the ears; one letter apart and unrelated in origin
entries.definitionCN: 用耳朵接收声音；只差一个字母，词源无关

entries.definition: the organ of hearing; fear without the f
entries.definitionCN: 听觉器官；即 fear 去掉 f

entries.definition: money paid for a journey; close in sound but a different root
entries.definitionCN: 车费；发音相近但词源不同

entries.definition: great fear of something that may happen
entries.definitionCN: 对将临之事的强烈恐惧

entries.definition: extreme and overwhelming fear
a state of nervous worry about the future
entries.definitionCN: 对未来的紧张忧虑；焦虑

normalIntro.en: Five handles from the family and the everyday phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 五个来自词族与日常短语的记忆抓手。

normal.en: fear has three letters f-e-a-r, like four quick heartbeats when danger appears.
normal.cn: fear 四个字母，像危险出现时的四次快速心跳。

normal.en: fearful means full of fear, fearless means without it: same root, opposite endings.
normal.cn: fearful 是充满恐惧，fearless 是毫无恐惧：同根而词尾相反。

normal.en: for fear of doing something means you avoid it to stay safe.
normal.cn: for fear of doing something 表示为安全起见而避免做某事。

normal.en: I fear so / I fear not is a polite way to say yes or no about bad news.
normal.cn: I fear so / I fear not 是对坏消息礼貌地说「恐怕是/恐怕不是」。

normal.en: German Gefahr means danger, a cousin from the same old root.
normal.cn: 德语 Gefahr 意为「危险」，是同一古老词根的亲戚。

abstract.en: Fear is a smoke alarm wired to your imagination, loud even when the fire is far away.
abstract.cn: 恐惧像接到想象上的烟雾报警器，火还很远就已经大响。

abstract.en: Dread is fear with a calendar: it counts the days to something bad.
abstract.cn: dread 是带日历的恐惧：它替你倒数坏日子的到来。

abstract.en: Awe is fear wearing a crown: the same alarm, pointed at greatness.
abstract.cn: 敬畏是戴王冠的恐惧：同一台警报，对准的是伟大。

examples.en: He overcame his fear of public speaking by practising weekly.
examples.cn: 他通过每周练习克服了当众讲话的恐惧。

examples.en: I fear that the train has already left.
examples.cn: 恐怕火车已经开走了。

examples.en: The villagers lived in fear of the flood every summer.
examples.cn: 村民每年夏天都生活在对洪水的恐惧中。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「菲尔怕」—— 菲尔一听到怪声就害怕 → fear 恐惧、害怕

root: 出自古英语 fer「突发的危险」，可上溯至重构的日耳曼词根（一般认为与表「危险、来袭」的语族相关）；词义由「危险」转为「对危险的感受」。

sensesIntro.en: From the raw feeling outward to specific worries, the verb of feeling, prediction of bad news, and awe.
sensesIntro.cn: 从原始情绪出发，扩展到具体顾虑、动词用法、对坏消息的料想以及敬畏。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a body frozen in the dark, eyes fixed on a possible danger.
core.cn: 核心意象：黑暗中僵住的身体，眼睛盯着可能的危险。

branches.en: THE FEELING: fear itself as emotion.
branches.cn: 情绪：恐惧这种感受本身。

branches.en: THE WORRY: a specific imagined bad event.
branches.cn: 顾虑：具体的、想象中的坏事。

branches.en: THE ACTION: being afraid as a verb.
THE PREDICTION: expecting the worst.
THE RESPECT: awe before power.

intro.en: Fear builds a compact family with two opposite adjectives and their adverbs.
intro.cn: fear 构成一个紧凑的词族：两个意义相反的形容词及其副词。

latinIntro.en: Fear has no Latin relatives; the family is purely Germanic, built with native suffixes.
latinIntro.cn: fear 没有拉丁同族词；词族纯出日耳曼本族，用本族后缀构成。

items.meaning: filled with fear or causing fear
items.example: A fearful crash woke the street.
items.exampleCN: 可怕的撞击声惊醒整条街。

items.example: The fearless reporter followed the story.
He whispered for fear of being heard.
items.exampleCN: 他压低声音以免被人听见。

items.example: Her fear of heights kept her inside.

definition_zh: 喂养；给……吃；喂奶；提供（信息、线索）；饲料；（社交媒体的）动态流
definition_en: to give food to a person, animal or machine, or to supply something such as information; also the food itself or a stream of updates
core_image: 一只摊开的手把食物送进张开的嘴里，链条一样把养分送下去
scene: 傍晚的农场里，父亲提着饲料桶走向鸡舍。He feeds the chickens before the sun goes down.
sceneCN: 这里 feed 是动词，指「给动物喂食」，对应第 1 个义项；句意为他在太阳落山前喂鸡。

pos.zh: 饲料；一餐；（社交媒体的）动态流

derivatives.zh: 饲养员；喂食器（feed 加施动者后缀 -er，指喂食的人或装置）
喂食；进食（feed 的动名词形式）
反馈（feed 与 back 复合，指信息的回传）

senses.title: To give food to a person or animal
senses.definition: to give food to someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 给某人或某物食物吃
senses.example: She feeds the baby with a spoon.
senses.exampleCN: 她用勺子喂婴儿。
senses.why: The picture is a hand carrying food to a mouth, so the basic sense is direct giving.
senses.whyCN: 画面是一只手把食物送到嘴边，因此基本义是直接的给予。

senses.title: To eat food
senses.definition: to eat, especially of animals
senses.definitionCN: 吃食物，多用于动物
senses.example: Cows feed on grass.
senses.exampleCN: 牛以草为食。
senses.why: If you can feed someone, the eater can be said to feed as well: the action points both ways.
senses.whyCN: 既然可以喂别人，进食的一方也可以说 feed：动作双向通用。

senses.title: To supply with information or material
senses.definition: to supply a machine, system or person with information, material or power
senses.definitionCN: 给机器、系统或人提供信息、材料或动力
senses.example: The sensors feed data to the computer.
senses.exampleCN: 传感器把数据传给计算机。
senses.why: Food entering a mouth and data entering a system are the same picture: something flows in.
senses.whyCN: 食物入口与数据入系统是同一画面：有东西源源流入。

senses.title: To support or encourage something bad
senses.definition: to make a feeling or situation stronger, especially a bad one
senses.definitionCN: 使某种情绪或局面变强，尤指坏的方面
senses.example: Rumours feed public panic.
senses.exampleCN: 谣言助长公众恐慌。
senses.why: A feeling is a mouth too: whatever you feed it, it grows.
senses.whyCN: 情绪也是一张嘴：喂什么，它就长什么。

senses.title: Food for animals
senses.definition: food given to animals
senses.definitionCN: 给动物吃的食物
senses.example: The farmer bought a bag of chicken feed.
senses.exampleCN: 农民买了一袋鸡饲料。
senses.why: The verb becomes a noun: the thing given is named after the giving.
senses.whyCN: 动词变名词：被给予之物以「给予」这个动作命名。

senses.title: A stream of updates
senses.definition: a continuous stream of updates or messages, especially online
senses.definitionCN: 持续不断的更新或消息流，多指网络
senses.example: My social media feed is full of cat videos.
senses.exampleCN: 我的社交媒体动态里全是猫的视频。
senses.why: The supply sense meets the internet: content flows to users like feed to animals.
senses.whyCN: 供给义遇上互联网：内容流向用户，就像饲料流向牲口。

intro.en: Feed is an old Germanic strong verb, tied to food and fodder, whose past tense fed has stayed stable for over a thousand years.
intro.cn: feed 是古老的日耳曼强变化动词，与 food、fodder 同源，过去式 fed 一千多年来保持稳定。

items.en: A reconstructed root fodam meant 'food, pasture'; it is the same stock that gives food and fodder.
items.cn: 一般认为，重构词根 fodam 意为「食物、牧场」；food（食物）与 fodder（饲料）同出一源。

items.en: Old English fedan meant 'to nourish, give food to', with past tense fede.
items.cn: 古英语 fedan 意为「滋养、给食」，过去式为 fede。

items.en: Middle English feden kept the strong past form fed and the sense of nourishing people and beasts.
items.cn: 中古英语 feden 保留强变化过去式 fed 及滋养人畜之义。

items.en: Modern English extended feed to machines, data, and feelings, and the noun grew for animal food.
items.cn: 现代英语把 feed 扩展到机器、数据与情绪，名词义指动物饲料。

items.en: The internet age added the news feed, where content streams continuously to users.
items.cn: 互联网时代又添了新闻推送义，内容持续不断地流向用户。

note.en: Look-alikes share the fed shape or the food root; near-meaning words cover giving food and supplying data.
note.cn: 形近组共享 fed 字形或 food 词根；近义组覆盖给食与供数两片义场。

entries.definition: things eaten; the noun cousin of feed
entries.definitionCN: 食物；与 feed 同根的名词亲戚

entries.definition: dry food for farm animals
to touch or sense; one letter apart but a different verb family
entries.definitionCN: 触摸或感觉；只差一个字母，属不同动词家族

entries.definition: to feed and help grow
to provide what is needed
to feed on grass in a field

normalIntro.en: Five handles from the food root and the modern data sense.
normalIntro.cn: 五个来自 food 词根与现代数据义的记忆抓手。

normal.en: feed and food share the old root: feeding is moving food along.
normal.cn: feed 与 food 同根：喂食就是把食物沿链条传递。

normal.en: The past tense is fed, not feeded: a strong verb that never changed.
normal.cn: 过去式是 fed，不是 feeded：从未变格的强变化动词。

normal.en: feed on means what an animal lives on, as cows feed on grass.
normal.cn: feed on 指动物以何为食，如牛吃草。

normal.en: feedback is information fed back to the source, one of the oldest loan ideas from engineering.
normal.cn: feedback 是把信息回传给源头，工程学传来的经典概念。

normal.en: A news feed keeps dropping content into your day, like a bucket that never empties.
normal.cn: 新闻推送不断往你一天里投放内容，像一个倒不空的桶。

abstract.en: Every feed is a pipe: whatever flows in, something grows at the far end.
abstract.cn: 每次喂送都是一条管道：流入什么，末端就长出什么。

abstract.en: Attention is the mouth of the mind; the feed decides the diet.
abstract.cn: 注意力是心灵之口，信息流决定精神食谱。

abstract.en: To feed a rumour is to water a weed: it grows overnight.
abstract.cn: 喂谣言如同给野草浇水：一夜疯长。

examples.en: The nurse feeds the patients who cannot move their hands.
examples.cn: 护士给不能动手的病人喂饭。

examples.en: The software feeds live prices to the trading system.
examples.cn: 软件向交易系统提供实时价格。

examples.en: Farmers store enough feed for the winter months.
examples.cn: 农民储备足够的饲料过冬。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「费的」—— 买饲料是要花钱（费）的，花了钱才能喂 → feed 喂养、饲料

root: 与 food、fodder 同出日耳曼语根（重构形式 fodam，一般认为表「食物」），经古英语 fedan「滋养」而来；核心是「把食物送下去」。

sensesIntro.en: From giving food outward to eating, supplying systems, fuelling feelings, animal food, and online streams.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「给食」扩展到进食、为系统供数、助长情绪、动物饲料与网络信息流。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an open hand carrying food down an open mouth.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只摊开的手把食物送进张开的嘴。

branches.en: GIVING: putting food into a mouth.
EATING: the receiving end of the same action.
branches.cn: 进食：同一动作的接收端。

branches.en: SUPPLY: feeding systems with data or power.
branches.cn: 供给：为系统提供数据或动力。

branches.en: MATERIAL: the food itself, for animals or machines.
branches.cn: 物料：食物本身，用于牲口或机器。

branches.en: THE STREAM: continuous content flowing to users.
branches.cn: 信息流：持续流向用户的内容。

intro.en: Feed forms compounds faster than affixes; the family lives on food words and data words.
intro.cn: feed 更多以复合构词见长；词族分布在食物词与数据词两端。

latinIntro.en: Feed is Germanic to the core; Latin used entirely different words for feeding, so there are no Latin siblings.
latinIntro.cn: feed 是纯正的日耳曼词；拉丁语用完全不同的词表喂食，因此没有拉丁同族词。

items.meaning: one who or that which feeds
items.example: A bird feeder hung in the tree.
items.exampleCN: 树上挂着一个鸟类喂食器。
老师给出了有用的反馈。

items.meaning: food for chickens; a tiny sum

definition_zh: 感觉；触摸；认为；觉得；触感；直觉
definition_en: to experience an emotion or physical sensation, to touch something, or to hold an opinion; also the sense of touch or a general impression
core_image: 指尖与皮肤成为世界的接口，触到什么、心里就升起什么
scene: 诊室里医生先搓热双手，再为病人检查患处。The doctor felt the patient's arm gently.
sceneCN: 这里 feel 是动词，指「用手触摸以检查」，对应第 3 个义项；句意为医生轻柔地触按病人的手臂。

derivatives.zh: 感觉；情感（feel 的动名词，指感受或情绪）
感情；情绪（feeling 的复数，多指心情）
触角；试探者（feel 加 -er，指起触觉作用的器官或试探之人）

senses.title: To experience an emotion
senses.definition: to experience a state of mind or emotion
senses.definitionCN: 经历某种心理或情绪状态
senses.example: I feel happy today.
senses.exampleCN: 我今天感到快乐。
senses.why: The inner world is known the way the outer one is touched, so emotion rides on the same verb.
senses.whyCN: 内心世界像外界一样被「摸到」，所以情绪也用同一个动词承载。

senses.title: To sense something physically
senses.definition: to notice something through the body or senses
senses.definitionCN: 通过身体或感官察觉某事
senses.example: She felt a pain in her back.
senses.exampleCN: 她感到背部疼痛。
senses.why: Sensation is the body's data stream, and feel is the verb that reports it.
senses.whyCN: 身体感受是身体的信号流，feel 就是报告它的动词。

senses.title: To touch something
senses.definition: to touch something with the fingers to learn about it
senses.definitionCN: 用手触碰以了解某物
senses.example: He felt the wall for the light switch.
senses.exampleCN: 他在墙上摸电灯开关。
senses.why: The hand searches where the eyes cannot, so the verb moves from sensing to touching.
senses.whyCN: 手在眼睛看不见处搜索，于是动词从「感知」滑向「触摸」。

senses.title: To hold an opinion
senses.definition: to have an opinion or belief about something
senses.definitionCN: 对某事持有看法或信念
senses.example: I feel that the plan is fair.
senses.exampleCN: 我认为这个计划是公平的。
senses.why: An opinion is a judgement you sense before you argue it, so thinking borrows the word.
senses.whyCN: 观点是先于论证被感知到的判断，所以思维借用了这个词。

senses.title: The sense of touch
senses.definition: the ability to feel things through the skin
senses.definitionCN: 通过皮肤感知事物的能力
senses.example: Fingertips give a fine sense of feel.
senses.exampleCN: 指尖提供精细的触觉。
senses.why: The verb freezes into a noun: the act of touching names the faculty itself.
senses.whyCN: 动词凝固为名词：触摸这一行为命名了触觉本身。

senses.title: A general impression or atmosphere
senses.definition: the impression a place or situation gives
senses.definitionCN: 某个地方或情境给人的总体印象
senses.example: The old town has a peaceful feel.
senses.exampleCN: 这座老城给人宁静的感觉。
senses.why: Everything you touch leaves a texture, and a place's mood is its texture.
senses.whyCN: 触过之物都留下质感，一个地方的氛围正是它的质感。

intro.en: Feel is a Germanic strong verb of touch and sensation, whose past tense felt has been stable since Old English.
intro.cn: feel 是日耳曼强变化动词，表触觉与感受，过去式 felt 自古英语以来一直稳定。

items.en: A reconstructed root foljan meant 'to perceive by touch'; related forms appear across Germanic languages.
items.cn: 一般认为，重构词根 foljan 意为「以触觉感知」；相关形式遍布日耳曼诸语。

items.en: Old English felan meant 'to touch, perceive', with the past participle folen.
items.cn: 古英语 felan 意为「触摸、感知」，过去分词为 folen。

items.en: Middle English len kept the strong forms and stretched the verb to emotions.
items.cn: 中古英语继续使用强变化形式，并把动词扩展到情绪领域。

items.en: The verb fixed as feel with felt as past form, covering body, heart and mind.
items.cn: 现代英语定为 feel，过去式 felt，覆盖身体、心灵与思维。

items.en: Modern usage added the noun feel for atmosphere, as in the feel of a place.
items.cn: 现代用法又给名词 feel 增加氛围义，如 the feel of a place。

note.en: Look-alikes differ by one letter; near-meaning words sit in the fields of touch, emotion and opinion.
note.cn: 形近组仅差一个字母；近义组分布于触觉、情绪与看法三个义场。

entries.definition: to give food; one letter apart and a different verb family
entries.definitionCN: 喂食；只差一个字母，属不同动词家族

entries.definition: to knock down, or the past of fall
entries.definitionCN: 砍倒，或 fall 的过去式；拼写仅一字母之差

entries.definition: the back of the foot; close in shape, unrelated in root
entries.definitionCN: 脚后跟；形状相近，词根无关

entries.definition: to notice through the senses or instinct
to put a hand on something
to notice or understand through the senses or mind
entries.definitionCN: 通过感官或心智察觉、领会

normalIntro.en: Five handles from the verb forms and the everyday phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 五个来自动词形式与日常短语的记忆抓手。

normal.en: feel / felt / felt: the ee becomes e, a regular strong-verb switch.
normal.cn: feel / felt / felt：ee 变 e，是规则元音交替。

normal.en: feel like doing means want to do it right now.
normal.cn: feel like doing 表示现在就想做某事。

normal.en: feel free to call means you may call without asking.
normal.cn: feel free to call 表示不必征询即可来电。

normal.en: feeling carries both body sensations and emotions in one word.
normal.cn: feeling 一个词兼指身体感觉与情绪。

normal.en: Never confuse feel with fell, which is to knock down.
normal.cn: 别把 feel 与 fell（砍倒）弄混。

abstract.en: Feel is the skin's way of reading the world, and the heart borrowed the alphabet.
abstract.cn: feel 是皮肤阅读世界的方式，心灵借用了这套字母。

abstract.en: Emotions are touches that never reach the hand.
abstract.cn: 情绪是到不了手上的触碰。

abstract.en: A place has a feel the way fabric has a weave: invisible but always there.
abstract.cn: 地方的氛围如同织物的纹理：看不见，却始终在场。

examples.en: Do you feel the draft coming from the window?
examples.cn: 你感觉到窗户那边透进的风了吗？

examples.en: She felt the fabric before buying the coat.
examples.cn: 买外套之前她先摸了摸面料。

examples.en: I feel that we should leave early to avoid traffic.
examples.cn: 我觉得我们该早点出发避开堵车。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「肥哦」—— 摸到肥肉软软的感觉 → feel 感觉、触摸

root: 出自古英语 felan「触摸、感知」，上溯重构的日耳曼词根 foljan（一般认为）；核心是「以身体为接口感知世界」。

sensesIntro.en: From body sensation outward to emotion, touching, opinion, the touch faculty, and atmosphere.
sensesIntro.cn: 从身体感觉扩展到情绪、触摸、观点、触觉能力与整体氛围。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: fingertips as the world's reading surface.
core.cn: 核心意象：指尖是世界的阅读面。

branches.en: SENSATION: what the body notices, inside or out.
branches.cn: 感受：身体内外察觉到的东西。

branches.en: TOUCHING: the hand exploring in the dark.
OPINION: a judgement sensed before it is argued.
branches.cn: 观点：先于论证被感知的判断。

branches.en: THE FACULTY: touch as an ability.
ATMOSPHERE: the texture of a place or moment.
branches.cn: 氛围：地方或时刻的质感。

intro.en: Feel keeps a short family: the noun feeling and a few compounds do most of the work.
intro.cn: feel 词族精简：名词 feeling 与少量复合词承担主要功能。

latinIntro.en: Latin used tangere and sentire, unrelated roots, so feel has no Latin siblings.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语用 tangere 与 sentire 表触知，词根无关，因此 feel 没有拉丁同族词。

items.meaning: an organ or tool for touching
to want or to seem like

items.example: He got the feel of the new car.
The cafe has a homey feel.
items.exampleCN: 这家咖啡馆很有温馨感。

items.example: She felt out their opinion first.
items.exampleCN: 她先试探了他们的意见。

items.meaning: to search by touch, or to sympathise
items.example: We all feel for the family.

definition_zh: 栅栏；篱笆；围栏；击剑运动；把……围起来；闪烁其词
definition_en: a structure made of posts and boards or wire that divides or surrounds an area, the sport of sword fighting, or to surround an area with such a structure
core_image: 一根根木桩连成线，把院子里的世界和外面的世界隔开
scene: 新搬来的邻居正沿着院界把木桩一根根打进土里。They will fence the yard to keep the dog inside.
sceneCN: 这里 fence 是动词，指「用栅栏把院子围起来」，对应第 4 个义项；句意为他们要给院子装栅栏，把狗关在院内。

pos.zh: 栅栏；篱笆；围栏；击剑运动
用栅栏围起；击剑；回避正面回答

derivatives.zh: 栅栏材料；击剑运动（fence 加 -ing，指围栏材料或剑术运动）
击剑运动员（fence 加施动者后缀 -er）
防御；保卫（与 fence 同源，拉丁语系内表「隔开、挡开」）

senses.title: A barrier around or between areas
senses.definition: a structure of posts, boards or wire that encloses or divides land
senses.definitionCN: 由木桩、木板或铁丝构成，用于围住或分隔土地的结构
senses.example: The horse jumped over the fence.
senses.exampleCN: 马跳过了栅栏。
senses.why: The word means the line itself first: posts joined into a boundary you can see.
senses.whyCN: 这个词首先指那条线本身：木桩连成看得见的边界。

senses.title: The sport of sword fighting
senses.definition: a sport in which two people fight with long thin swords
senses.definitionCN: 两名选手用细长剑对抗的运动
senses.example: He took up fencing at school.
senses.exampleCN: 他在学校开始练击剑。
senses.why: Sword fighting grew out of defending a line, so the barrier word named the sport.
senses.whyCN: 剑术源于守住一条线，于是围栏词命名了这项运动。

senses.title: To avoid giving a direct answer
senses.definition: to answer questions in a clever but unclear way
senses.definitionCN: 用巧妙但含糊的方式回答问题
senses.example: The minister fenced when asked about taxes.
senses.exampleCN: 被问到税收时，部长闪烁其词。
senses.why: A fencer parries every blow, so the verb describes dodging every question.
senses.whyCN: 击剑手挡开每一次攻击，动词因此形容躲开每一个问题。

senses.title: To surround an area with a fence
senses.definition: to put a fence around a garden or field
senses.definitionCN: 在花园或田地四周装上栅栏
senses.example: They fenced the yard to keep the dog inside.
senses.exampleCN: 他们给院子装上栅栏，把狗关在里面。
senses.why: The noun turns into an action: putting the line into place.
senses.whyCN: 名词转为动作：把那条边界线装到位。

senses.title: To separate off a piece of land
senses.definition: to divide land with a fence, often into a separate part
senses.definitionCN: 用栅栏把土地隔成单独的部分
senses.example: Part of the field was fenced off for repairs.
senses.exampleCN: 田地的一部分被隔开进行修缮。
senses.why: A barrier does not only enclose; it also cuts one space away from another.
senses.whyCN: 栅栏不只围住，也把一处空间从另一处切分出来。

intro.en: Fence is a shortened form of defence: the same idea of shielding a line was cut down to name the barrier, then the swordplay behind it.
intro.cn: fence 是 defence 的缩略：同属「挡开、护住一条线」的概念被截短用来命名栅栏，随后又指栅栏后的剑术。

items.en: Latin defendere meant 'to ward off, guard', built from fens, the stem of fendere 'to strike'.
items.cn: 拉丁语 defendere 意为「挡开、守护」，出自 fendere「击打」的词干 fens。

items.en: Old French defence carried the idea of guarding and shielding into Romance speech.
items.cn: 古法语 defence 把守护与遮挡的观念带入罗曼语。

items.en: Middle English shortened defence to fense, written fence, for a protective barrier.
items.cn: 中古英语把 defence 缩略为 fense，写作 fence，指防护性屏障。

items.en: The barrier sense spread to farms and gardens, and the verb fence meant to enclose.
items.cn: 现代英语里屏障义扩展到农田与花园，动词 fence 表示围起。

items.en: Sword practice and clever parrying gave the sport, the athlete and the evasive answer senses.
items.cn: 剑术练习与巧妙的挡避派生出运动、运动员与回避作答诸义。

note.en: Look-alikes share the fence spelling or the fend root; near-meaning words cover barriers and evasion.
note.cn: 形近组共享 fence 拼写或 fend 词根；近义组覆盖屏障与回避两个义场。

entries.definition: the act of protecting; fence is its shortened form
a crime or hurt feeling; close in shape but about attacking, not barriers
entries.definitionCN: 犯罪或冒犯；形近而义指冒犯，与屏障无关

entries.definition: a guard against scratches; keeps the fend idea
entries.definitionCN: 防擦护板；保留 fend 的「挡开」义

entries.definition: a row of bushes used as a boundary
a solid structure dividing spaces
to avoid giving a direct answer
entries.definitionCN: 回避；躲闪不作正面回答

normalIntro.en: Five handles from the defence root and the classic phrase.
normalIntro.cn: 五个来自 defence 词根与经典短语的记忆抓手。

normal.en: fence is defence with the de- sliced off: a fence defends your line.
normal.cn: fence 是 defence 砍掉 de-：栅栏守住你的边界。

normal.en: sit on the fence is the picture of a person sitting on a wall between two sides.
normal.cn: sit on the fence 画面是一个人坐在两侧之间的墙上骑墙观望。

normal.en: fencing is the sport, fencer is the athlete, fence is the sword move.
normal.cn: fencing 是运动，fencer 是运动员，fence 是剑上动作。

normal.en: fence off means to cut a piece of land away with a barrier.
normal.cn: fence off 表示用栅栏把一块地隔出来。

normal.en: to fence in a question is to parry it like a sword blow.
normal.cn: 在问题上 fence in，就像用剑挡开劈来的一击。

abstract.en: A fence is an opinion you can see: it says here, not there.
abstract.cn: 栅栏是一条看得见的立场：宣告这里，而非那里。

abstract.en: Fencing words, like fencing swords, keep the fight going without landing anywhere.
abstract.cn: 闪避的言辞如同击剑的剑，打来打去却从不落在实处。

abstract.en: Every boundary is both a shield and a statement.
abstract.cn: 每一条边界既是盾牌，也是宣告。

examples.en: The sheep escaped through a hole in the fence.
examples.cn: 羊从栅栏的破洞里跑出去了。

examples.en: She fenced off the vegetable patch to protect it from rabbits.
examples.cn: 她用栅栏把菜圃隔开，防止兔子进来。

examples.en: Reporters pressed him for answers, but he kept fencing.
examples.cn: 记者们追问答案，他却一直闪避。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「奋死」—— 守卫边界奋死不让 → fence 栅栏；捍卫

root: fence 是 defence 的缩略形，源自拉丁语 defendere「挡开、守护」（词干 fens，出自 fendere「击打」），经古法语 defence 进入中古英语后截短而成。

sensesIntro.en: From the barrier itself to the sword sport, evasive answers, and the acts of enclosing and dividing.
sensesIntro.cn: 从屏障本身到击剑运动、闪避作答，以及围起与隔开两个动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: posts joined into a visible line that separates inside from outside.
core.cn: 核心意象：木桩连成一条可见的线，隔开内与外。

branches.en: THE LINE: the physical barrier.
THE SPORT: swordplay born of defence.
THE PARRY: dodging questions like blows.
branches.cn: 挡避：像挡剑一样躲开问题。

branches.en: THE ACT: putting a fence in place.
THE CUT: dividing land into parts.

intro.en: The fence family hangs on the fend root, where defence, offence and their verbs meet.
intro.cn: fence 词族挂在 fend 词根上，defence、offence 及其动词在此交汇。

latinIntro.en: Latin fendere 'to strike' gives the stems; defendere adds the prefix de- 'away'.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 fendere「击打」提供词干；defendere 加上前缀 de-「离开」。

items.meaning: to strike against; to hurt feelings
items.exampleCN: 他的玩笑冒犯了许多人。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 被击打的；fence 的词干来源

definition_zh: 节日；节期；庆典；会演；（音乐、电影等的）节
definition_en: a special day or period of celebration, or an organized series of performances or events
core_image: 街道挂满彩灯与旗帜，人们从四面八方涌向同一片欢腾
scene: 元宵夜，孩子们提着灯笼挤在挂满灯谜的长街上。The lantern festival draws crowds from every part of the city.
sceneCN: 这里 festival 是名词，指「节庆活动」，对应第 1 个义项；句意为灯会吸引了全城各处的人潮。

derivatives.zh: 节日的；欢庆的（festival 的词根加形容词后缀 -ive，指充满节日气氛）
庆典；欢庆活动（festive 加名词后缀 -ity，指欢乐的庆祝）
庆祝活动（festivity 的复数，指一系列庆祝）

senses.title: A special day of celebration
senses.definition: a special day or period when people celebrate something
senses.definitionCN: 人们举行庆祝的特殊日子或时段
senses.example: The Spring Festival is the biggest holiday in China.
senses.exampleCN: 春节是中国最大的节日。
senses.why: A fixed date turns ordinary time into a marked moment, so the word names the day itself.
senses.whyCN: 固定的日期把平常时光变成被标记的时刻，所以词首先指那个日子。

senses.title: An organized series of events
senses.definition: an organized set of performances, films or competitions held over several days
senses.definitionCN: 连日举行的表演、电影或比赛的系列安排
senses.example: The town hosts a jazz festival every summer.
senses.exampleCN: 小镇每年夏天举办爵士音乐节。
senses.why: When the celebration becomes a programme, the day grows into an event series.
senses.whyCN: 当庆祝变成节目单，单日就扩展成系列活动。

senses.title: The joyful atmosphere of celebration
senses.definition: the lively mood and activities of a celebration
senses.definitionCN: 庆祝时的热闹气氛与活动
senses.example: The whole street was in festival mood.
senses.exampleCN: 整条街都沉浸在节日的欢乐中。
senses.why: The day is felt as much as marked: the word covers the mood it creates.
senses.whyCN: 节日既被标记也被感受：这个词也涵盖它制造的气氛。

intro.en: Festival descends from Latin festus 'of a feast, joyful', the same root that gives feast, and it arrived through Old French as both day and celebration.
intro.cn: festival 源自拉丁语 festus「宴会的、欢乐的」，与 feast 同根，经古法语传入，兼指日子与庆典。

items.en: Festus meant 'of a feast, joyous', marking days set aside for worship and meals.
items.cn: festus 意为「宴会的、欢乐的」，标记专用于祭拜与宴饮的日子。

items.en: Medieval Latin festum meant 'a feast day', the direct source of both feast and festival.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 festum 意为「节日」，是 feast 与 festival 的直接来源。

items.en: Old French feste kept the religious feast day sense.
items.cn: 古法语 feste 保留了宗教节日义。

items.en: Middle English borrowed feste as feast, and festival came later through the adjective line.
items.cn: 中古英语把 feste 借为 feast，festival 则经由形容词路线较晚到来。

items.en: Modern English uses festival for holidays and for organized event series like film festivals.
items.cn: 现代英语用 festival 指节日及电影节之类的系列活动。

note.en: Look-alikes share the fest root; near-meaning words cover holidays and public celebrations.
note.cn: 形近组共享 fest 词根；近义组覆盖假日与公共庆典。

entries.definition: a large special meal; from the same Latin line
full of celebration; the adjective cousin
entries.definitionCN: 节日的；欢乐的；形容词同族

entries.definition: a person who attends festivals
a day of rest or celebration
a public festival with parries and costumes
entries.definitionCN: 有游行与装束的狂欢节

entries.definition: the act of celebrating an event

normalIntro.en: Five handles from the fest root and common festival types.
normalIntro.cn: 五个来自 fest 词根与常见节庆类型的记忆抓手。

normal.en: festival and feast share the root fest: a festival is a feast of days.
normal.cn: festival 与 feast 同含词根 fest：节日就是日子的盛宴。

normal.en: music festival, film festival: any art can fill the calendar.
normal.cn: music festival、film festival：任何艺术都能填满节庆日历。

normal.en: festive is the adjective: festive lights make a festival street.
normal.cn: festive 是形容词：节日的彩灯造就节日的街道。

normal.en: the root festus meant joyful, so every festival promises joy.
normal.cn: 词根 festus 本义欢乐，所以每个节日都许诺欢乐。

normal.en: harvest festival thanks the fields; spring festival welcomes the year.
normal.cn: 丰收节感谢田地，春节迎接新年。

abstract.en: A festival is a knot in time where many threads of joy are tied together.
abstract.cn: 节日是时间上的一个结，把许多欢乐的线系在一起。

abstract.en: Festivals are calendars rehearsing happiness.
abstract.cn: 节日是日历在排练幸福。

abstract.en: In festival mood, the street itself wears a costume.
abstract.cn: 节日气氛里，街道自己也穿上了盛装。

examples.en: Families gather for dinner during the Mid-Autumn Festival.
examples.cn: 中秋节期间家家户户团聚吃饭。

examples.en: Her short film won an award at the festival.
examples.cn: 她的短片在电影节上获了奖。

examples.en: The square took on a festival air with music and dancing.
examples.cn: 广场上音乐与舞蹈让整个会场充满节日气氛。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「饭吃我哦」—— 过节大家争着请客，饭吃我哦 → festival 节日

root: 源自拉丁语 festus「宴会的、欢乐的」，经中世纪拉丁语 festum「节日」与古法语 feste 传入英语；与 feast 同根，核心是「欢乐的固定日子」。

sensesIntro.en: From the marked celebration day to organized event series and the joyful mood itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 从被标记的庆祝日，到系列会演活动，再到节日的欢乐气氛。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a street under lanterns and flags, all roads leading to one celebration.
core.cn: 核心意象：灯笼与彩旗下的街道，条条路通向同一场欢庆。

branches.en: THE DAY: a date fixed for celebration.
THE PROGRAMME: a series of events and shows.
branches.cn: 节目单：连日的活动与会演。

branches.en: THE MOOD: the joy the day produces.
THE TRADITION: festivals repeated year after year.
THE STAGE: arts festivals that gather performers.
branches.cn: 舞台：聚集表演者的艺术节。

intro.en: The fest root builds a compact family of days, meals and moods.
intro.cn: fest 词根构成一个紧凑词族，覆盖日子、宴席与气氛。

latinIntro.en: Latin festus 'joyous, of a feast' feeds feast, festive and festival alike.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 festus「欢乐的、宴会的」同时供给 feast、festive 与 festival。

items.structure: from Latin festum via Old French

items.example: The hall wore a festal look.

definition_zh: 发烧；发热；热病；狂热；亢奋
definition_en: a body temperature higher than normal because of illness, a disease marked by this, or a state of intense excitement
core_image: 额头滚烫，脸颊发红，整个身体像一团过热的炉火
scene: 深夜的孩子满脸通红，母亲把体温计贴上额头。The nurse checked whether the fever had broken.
sceneCN: 这里 fever 是名词，指「发烧」这一症状，对应第 1 个义项；句意为护士查看烧是否已经退去。

pos.zh: 发烧；热病；狂热；一时的亢奋

derivatives.zh: 发烧的；狂热的（fever 加形容词后缀 -ish，指体温高或情绪亢奋）
发烧地；狂热地（feverish 加副词后缀 -ly）
发烧的；焦躁的（fever 的过去分词作形容词，指受热或受扰的）

senses.title: A higher-than-normal body temperature
senses.definition: a body temperature above the normal level, usually from illness
senses.definitionCN: 体温高出正常水平，通常由疾病引起
senses.example: The child has a slight fever.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子有点低烧。
senses.why: The body burns hotter than it should, so the word names the heat itself.
senses.whyCN: 身体烧得比该有的温度高，词首先命名这股热度。

senses.title: A disease marked by fever
senses.definition: an illness in which fever is the main sign
senses.definitionCN: 以发热为主要征兆的疾病
senses.example: Scarlet fever once frightened every parent.
senses.exampleCN: 猩红热曾令每位家长恐惧。
senses.why: When the symptom defines the sickness, the sickness takes the symptom's name.
senses.whyCN: 当症状定义疾病，疾病便以症状为名。

senses.title: Intense excitement or agitation
senses.definition: a state of great excitement or nervous energy
senses.definitionCN: 极度兴奋或躁动的状态
senses.example: The city was in a fever of excitement before the match.
senses.exampleCN: 比赛前全城兴奋若狂。
senses.why: Excitement heats the mind the way illness heats the body.
senses.whyCN: 亢奋使头脑发热，正如疾病使身体发热。

senses.title: A short-lived craze
senses.definition: a wave of enthusiasm that sweeps through people for a time
senses.definitionCN: 一时席卷人群的热情浪潮
senses.example: Gold fever sent thousands west.
senses.exampleCN: 淘金热把成千上万的人推向西部。
senses.why: A craze is a fever of the crowd: it burns hot and passes.
senses.whyCN: 热潮是群体的发烧：烧得猛，退得也快。

intro.en: Fever comes straight from Latin febris 'heat of illness', borrowed through Old French fievre and reshaped into English spelling.
intro.cn: fever 直接源自拉丁语 febris「病热」，经古法语 fievre 借入并改写为英语拼写。

items.en: Latin febris meant 'fever', from a root meaning 'to burn'.
items.cn: 拉丁语 febris 意为「发烧」，出自表「燃烧」的词根。

items.en: Old French fievre carried the word into Romance speech with its senses intact.
items.cn: 古法语 fievre 原义不变地把这个词带入罗曼语。

items.en: Middle English adopted fever (also fevre) for body heat and for diseases like it.
items.cn: 中古英语借入 fever（亦作 fevre），指体热及类似疾病。

items.en: The spelling settled as fever, standard in medicine and daily speech.
items.cn: 现代英语拼写定为 fever，为医学与日常通用。

items.en: Metaphorical use spread widely: election fever, gold fever, a fever of activity.
items.cn: 比喻用法广泛传播：election fever、gold fever、a fever of activity。

note.en: Look-alikes share the fe- shape; near-meaning words cover temperature, illness and excitement.
note.cn: 形近组共享 fe- 字形；近义组覆盖体温、疾病与亢奋。

entries.definition: a smaller number of; one letter changes the meaning completely
entries.definitionCN: 更少的；仅一字母之差而意义全变

entries.definition: showing strong feeling; from Latin fervere 'to boil'
entries.definitionCN: 热烈的；出自拉丁语 fervere「沸腾」

entries.definition: a boat that carries people across water
entries.definitionCN: 渡船；拼写相近但词源无关

entries.definition: the degree of heat of the body
high temperature or hotness
a short-lived enthusiasm

normalIntro.en: Five handles from the Latin root and the metaphorical uses.
normalIntro.cn: 五个来自拉丁词根与比喻用法的记忆抓手。

normal.en: feverish means fever-like: hot body or hot mood.
normal.cn: feverish 意为「像发烧一样」：身体发热或情绪亢奋。

normal.en: break a fever means the fever finally stops.
normal.cn: break a fever 表示烧终于退了。

normal.en: gold fever is the classic crowd fever: everyone rushes for the same prize.
normal.cn: gold fever 是经典的群体狂热：人人涌向同一目标。

normal.en: Latin febris is the root; English fever keeps only the heat idea.
normal.cn: 词根是拉丁语 febris；英语 fever 只保留「热」的概念。

normal.en: never confuse fever with fewer, which counts things down.
normal.cn: 别把 fever 与 fewer（更少）弄混。

abstract.en: A fever is the body's alarm fire: hot, bright, and meant to pass.
abstract.cn: 发烧是身体的报警之火：灼热、明亮，也注定退去。

abstract.en: Crowd fever is a fire that spreads without fuel.
abstract.cn: 群体狂热是不需燃料也能蔓延的火。

abstract.en: Excitement and illness share one thermometer.
abstract.cn: 亢奋与疾病共用同一支体温计。

examples.en: His fever finally broke on the third night.
examples.cn: 他的烧在第三晚终于退了。

examples.en: The whole class was in a fever before the results were posted.
examples.cn: 成绩公布前全班都处于亢奋之中。

examples.en: Doctors warned that scarlet fever was spreading in the district.
examples.cn: 医生警告猩红热正在该地区蔓延。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「肥捂热」—— 发烧的人身体肥而滚烫，需捂热降温 → fever 发烧

root: 源自拉丁语 febris「发烧」（一般认为出自表「燃烧」的词根），经古法语 fievre 进入中古英语；核心是「病中之热」，后扩展为比喻的「狂热」。

sensesIntro.en: From body heat outward to the diseases named by it, and then to excitement and crowd crazes.
sensesIntro.cn: 从体温升高出发，扩展到以其命名之疾病，再到亢奋与群体热潮。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a burning forehead, the body running hotter than it should.
core.cn: 核心意象：滚烫的额头，身体烧得超过了应有的温度。

branches.en: THE HEAT: raised body temperature.
THE ILLNESS: disease known by its fever.
THE EXCITEMENT: minds heated like bodies.
branches.cn: 亢奋：头脑如身体般发热。

branches.en: THE CRAZE: a wave that burns and fades.
branches.cn: 热潮：烧起又退去的浪潮。

branches.en: THE METAPHOR: heat transferred from body to mood.
branches.cn: 比喻：热度由身体移入情绪。

intro.en: Fever builds its family with native suffixes: feverish, fevered and their adverbs.
intro.cn: fever 用本族后缀构词：feverish、fevered 及其副词。

latinIntro.en: Latin febris stands alone in the family; related Latin fervere 'to boil' gives fervent instead.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 febris 在词族中独立；相关的 fervere「沸腾」派生的是 fervent。

items.meaning: having a fever or wild excitement

items.exampleCN: 热烈的演讲打动了他们。

items.example: She caught a fever at camp.
A high fever needs a doctor.

definition_zh: 很少的；几乎没有的；少数的；很少；一些（a few）
definition_en: a small number of something, or hardly any at all; with a, a small number that does exist
core_image: 一大盘糖果被拿走后盘底只剩三五颗
scene: 野餐结束，桌上只剩零星几块饼干。Few students stayed after the lecture ended.
sceneCN: 这里 few 是限定词，指「几乎没有的」，对应第 1 个义项；句意为讲座结束后几乎没留下什么学生。

pos.zh: 很少的；几乎没有的；少数的

derivatives.zh: 少量；稀少（few 加名词后缀 -ness，指数量之小）
更少的（few 的比较级，用于可数名词）
最少的（few 的最高级）

senses.title: Hardly any
senses.definition: a surprisingly small number, emphasizing the lack
senses.definitionCN: 数量出奇地小，强调缺乏
senses.example: Few roads reach the village in winter.
senses.exampleCN: 冬天几乎没什么路能通到村子。
senses.why: The word leans on what is missing: the handful on the plate is named as a lack.
senses.whyCN: 这个词落在「缺」上：盘中剩的几颗被说成匮乏。

senses.title: A small number that exists
senses.definition: a small but real number of things
senses.definitionCN: 数量虽小但确实存在的几个
senses.example: Give me a few minutes to finish.
senses.exampleCN: 给我几分钟收尾。
senses.why: Adding a turns the lack into a small gift: some, though not many.
senses.whyCN: 加上 a，匮乏变成小小的一份：有一些，虽不多。

senses.title: A minority of people or things
senses.definition: a small group as opposed to the majority
senses.definitionCN: 相对于多数的小群体
senses.example: Power rested in the hands of the few.
senses.exampleCN: 权力掌握在少数人手中。
senses.why: The adjective hardens into a noun: the small group itself.
senses.whyCN: 形容词凝固为名词：那个小群体本身。

senses.title: A reduced number in comparison
senses.definition: a smaller number than before or than another group
senses.definitionCN: 比之前或比另一群体更少的数量
senses.example: Fewer cars means cleaner air.
senses.exampleCN: 车更少意味着空气更干净。
senses.why: Comparison stretches the word: the handful measured against a larger whole.
senses.whyCN: 比较拉伸词义：把那一小把放到更大的整体中衡量。

intro.en: Few is a native Germanic word, ancient and short, meaning 'small in number' since before written English.
intro.cn: few 是日耳曼本族的古老短词，早在书面英语出现之前就表示「数量少」。

items.en: A reconstructed root fawaz meant 'small, few'; cousins appear in Old Saxon and Gothic.
items.cn: 一般认为，重构词根 fawaz 意为「少的」；古撒克逊语与哥特语中有同族词。

items.en: Old English feawe (plural) meant 'few, little in number', used mainly with plural nouns.
items.cn: 古英语 feawe（复数形式）意为「少的」，主要与复数名词连用。

items.en: Middle English developed the a few phrase, separating 'hardly any' from 'some'.
items.cn: 中古英语发展出 a few 短语，把「几乎没有」与「有一些」分开。

items.en: Fewer and fewest fixed the comparison, kept strictly for countable things.
items.cn: 现代英语定下 fewer 与 fewest，严格用于可数名词的比较。

items.en: Phrases like quite a few and the few became idioms of number and class.
items.cn: quite a few 与 the few 等短语成为表数量与阶层的习语。

note.en: Look-alikes share the fe- shape; near-meaning words cover small numbers and scarcity.
note.cn: 形近组共享 fe- 字形；近义组覆盖小数量与稀少。

entries.definition: money paid for a service; unrelated in root
the comparative of few
what can be seen; different root, similar sound
entries.definitionCN: 景色；看法；词根不同而音近

entries.definition: not enough or hard to find
more than two but not many
entries.definitionCN: 几个；三个以上而不到许多

entries.definition: extra or minimal in amount

normalIntro.en: Five handles from the pairs and idioms of number.
normalIntro.cn: 五个来自数量搭配与习语的记忆抓手。

normal.en: few means almost none; a few means some: the a changes everything.
normal.cn: few 意为几乎没有；a few 意为有一些：一个 a 改变一切。

normal.en: fewer is for things you can count; less is for what you cannot.
normal.cn: fewer 用于可数名词；less 用于不可数。

normal.en: quite a few surprisingly means quite a lot.
normal.cn: quite a few 出人意料地表示「相当多」。

normal.en: the few names a chosen or lucky minority.
normal.cn: the few 指被选中或幸运的少数人。

normal.en: every few minutes means one gap of a few minutes between each event.
normal.cn: every few minutes 表示每隔几分钟一次。

abstract.en: Few is the sound of an empty jar: a small rattle at the bottom.
abstract.cn: few 是空罐子的声音：罐底稀疏的晃荡。

abstract.en: A few is the sound of a nearly empty jar that still has something to offer.
abstract.cn: a few 是罐子虽空却仍有余响。

abstract.en: Scarcity sharpens value: what few can hold, many will want.
abstract.cn: 稀缺抬升价值：少数人拥有的，多数人渴望。

examples.en: Few visitors come to the museum on rainy days.
examples.cn: 雨天来博物馆的访客寥寥无几。

examples.en: She answered the questions in a few clear sentences.
examples.cn: 她用寥寥几句就把问题讲清楚了。

examples.en: The law serves the many, not the few.
examples.cn: 法律服务于多数人，而非少数人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「夫优」—— 岗位少、竞争者多，夫优者胜 → few 很少的

root: 日耳曼本族词，出自重构词根 fawaz「少的」，经古英语 feawe「少的」沿用至今；核心是「数量之小」，并以 a few 区分「有些」。

sensesIntro.en: From the bare lack outward to a small existing number, the minority noun, and the comparative form.
sensesIntro.cn: 从纯粹的匮乏，到确实存在的小数目、表少数的名词，以及比较级形式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an almost-empty plate after the crowd has taken its share.
core.cn: 核心意象：人群取食后近乎见底的盘子。

branches.en: THE LACK: fewer than expected.
THE HANDFUL: a small number that still exists.
branches.cn: 一小把：确实存在的少量。

branches.en: THE MINORITY: the group of few people.
THE SCALE: measured against a larger whole.
THE ELITE: the few who hold what many lack.
branches.cn: 精英：拥有多数人所缺之物的少数。

intro.en: Few keeps a bare Germanic family: comparison forms and one abstract noun.
intro.cn: few 的日耳曼词族极简：比较级形式与一个抽象名词。

latinIntro.en: Few has no Latin relatives; Latin used paucus, which gives paucity instead.
latinIntro.cn: few 没有拉丁同族词；拉丁语用 paucus，派生出 paucity 一系。

items.example: The fewness of options troubled her.
Quite a few joined the trip.
items.exampleCN: 相当多的人参加了旅行。

items.example: Opinions split between the many and the few.
items.exampleCN: 意见在多数与少数间分裂。

items.example: A paucity of data limits the study.
He summed it up in a few words.

items.meaning: at intervals of a few days
items.example: Every few days a letter arrived.

definition_zh: 田地；田野；场地；领域；战场；运动场；（物理）场
definition_en: an area of open land for crops or animals, a piece of ground used for something, or a subject of study or activity
core_image: 一块被犁沟划分的开阔土地，风吹过整片绿色
scene: 清晨的农场上薄雾未散，拖拉机已驶入垄间。The wheat field stretches to the far woods.
sceneCN: 这里 field 是名词，指「田地」，对应第 1 个义项；句意为麦田一直延伸到远处的树林。

pos.zh: 田地；场地；领域；战场；（物理）场

collocations.zh: 到处沾花惹草；同时与多人交往

derivatives.zh: 外野手；守场员（field 加施动者后缀 -er，指守备球员）
实地调查；田野工作（field 与 work 复合，指在实地进行的研究）
守备；外场接球（field 的动名词）

senses.title: Open land for crops or animals
senses.definition: an area of land, often fenced, used for crops or grazing
senses.definitionCN: 用于种植庄稼或放牧的一块地，常有围栏
senses.example: Cows grazed in the green field.
senses.exampleCN: 牛群在绿野上吃草。
senses.why: The oldest picture is open ground with a boundary: land put to use.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的画面是有边界的开阔土地：被派上用场的地。

senses.title: An area of ground for games or battle
senses.definition: a piece of ground used for sports or fighting
senses.definitionCN: 用于运动或作战的地面
senses.example: The team ran onto the field.
senses.exampleCN: 球队跑进场地。
senses.why: Any land with a purpose becomes a field: play, battle, work.
senses.whyCN: 有用途的土地都成为 field：比赛、作战、劳作。

senses.title: A subject of study or work
senses.definition: a branch of knowledge or professional activity
senses.definitionCN: 一门学问或职业活动的分支
senses.example: She is a leader in the field of medicine.
senses.exampleCN: 她是医学界的领军人物。
senses.why: A career is a plot of land too: you work your own patch of knowledge.
senses.whyCN: 事业也是一块地：你在自己那片知识田里耕耘。

senses.title: A region of physical force
senses.definition: a region in which a force such as gravity acts
senses.definitionCN: 重力等力发生作用的区域
senses.example: The magnets created a strong field.
senses.exampleCN: 磁铁形成了强磁场。
senses.why: Science borrowed the agricultural picture: an invisible zone you can map.
senses.whyCN: 科学借来农耕画面：一块可以描绘的无形区域。

senses.title: To catch or deal with something
senses.definition: to catch a ball, or to deal with questions or a situation
senses.definitionCN: 接住球，或应对问题与局面
senses.example: He fielded every question with calm.
senses.exampleCN: 他沉着应对每一个问题。
senses.why: Standing in the field, you receive what comes: balls, or hard questions.
senses.whyCN: 守在场地上的人要接住来物：球，或刁钻的问题。

intro.en: Field is an ancient Germanic word for open or cleared land, sharing a root with the idea of flat ground.
intro.cn: field 是表示开阔或开垦土地的古老日耳曼词，与「平地」概念同根。

items.en: A reconstructed root felthuz meant 'flat land, plain'; Dutch veld and German Feld are cousins.
items.cn: 一般认为，重构词根 felthuz 意为「平地、平原」；荷兰语 veld 与德语 Feld 是同族词。

items.en: Old English feld meant 'open land, plain without woods', next to cleared ground.
items.cn: 古英语 feld 意为「旷野、无林平地」，与垦地相邻。

items.en: Middle English used field for farmland, battlefields and open country alike.
items.cn: 中古英语用 field 兼指农田、战场与旷野。

items.en: The word spread to sports grounds and branches of knowledge.
items.cn: 现代英语将其扩展到运动场与学问分支。

items.en: Nineteenth-century physics borrowed field for regions of magnetic and gravitational force.
items.cn: 十九世纪物理学借 field 指磁场与引力场所在的区域。

note.en: Look-alikes differ by one letter; near-meaning words cover land, domains and playing grounds.
note.cn: 形近组仅差一个字母；近义组覆盖土地、领域与运动场地。

entries.definition: the frequent wrong spelling of field
the past of hold; letters shifted but meaning far away
entries.definitionCN: hold 的过去式；字母换位而意义相远

entries.definition: the past form of field as a verb
grassland, often for hay
an area of knowledge or control
a stage for contests or debate

normalIntro.en: Five handles from the compounds and the metaphors.
normalIntro.cn: 五个来自复合词与比喻用法的记忆抓手。

normal.en: field trip takes the class out of school into the open land.
normal.cn: field trip 把课堂搬到开阔的野外。

normal.en: in the field of medicine means inside that domain of work.
normal.cn: in the field of medicine 表示身处医学这一领域。

normal.en: fielder and fielding belong to cricket and baseball talk.
normal.cn: fielder 与 fielding 属于板球与棒球用语。

normal.en: physics borrowed the word: magnetic field is an invisible field of force.
normal.cn: 物理学借用了这个词：磁场是一片无形的力场。

normal.en: old German Feld is the same word: flat open land.
normal.cn: 德语 Feld 与之同词：平坦开阔之地。

abstract.en: A field is land with a purpose drawn around it.
abstract.cn: field 是被目的圈出来的土地。

abstract.en: Every career is a field you plough with daily work.
abstract.cn: 每个职业都是你日日耕耘的田。

abstract.en: A field of force is land you cannot see but can only measure.
abstract.cn: 力场是看不见、只能测量的大地。

examples.en: The farmer fenced the field before spring planting.
examples.cn: 农民在春耕前给田地围上了栅栏。

examples.en: She answered the reporter's questions on the field of economics.
examples.cn: 她在经济学领域内回答了记者的提问。

examples.en: The shortstop fielded the ball cleanly and threw to first base.
examples.cn: 游击手稳稳接球并传向一垒。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「肥沃的」—— 田地肥沃才能有好收成 → field 田地、领域

root: 出自古英语 feld「旷野、垦地」，上溯重构日耳曼词根 felthuz「平地」；德语 Feld、荷兰语 veld 同族；核心是「有边界的开阔用地」。

sensesIntro.en: From farmland outward to sports and battle grounds, branches of knowledge, fields of force, and the act of receiving.
sensesIntro.cn: 从农田扩展到运动场与战场、学问分支、物理力场，以及接应这一动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: open flat land drawn into a useful boundary.
core.cn: 核心意象：被圈出用途的开阔平地。

branches.en: THE LAND: ground for crops and animals.
THE GROUND: play and battle on marked earth.
branches.cn: 场地：画线用于比赛或作战。

branches.en: THE DOMAIN: a subject you can work in.
THE FORCE: an invisible region science maps.
branches.cn: 力场：科学描绘的无形区域。

branches.en: THE CATCH: receiving what comes at you.

intro.en: Field prefers compounds: fieldwork, field trip, fielder and more.

intro.en: Fifteen is a pure Germanic compound: five plus ten, glued together in Old English and unchanged for a thousand years.
intro.cn: fifteen 是纯粹的日耳曼复合词：五加十，在古英语中拼合而成，一千年来保持不变。

items.en: Germanic counting built teens by adding the suffix -tein, 'ten', to each unit number.

items.en: Old English fiftene literally meant 'five-ten', spoken as one word.

items.en: Middle English kept the compound with a shifted stress: fif-TEEN.
items.cn: 中古英语保留复合词，重音移至后部：fif-TEEN。

items.en: Modern spelling fixed as fifteen, distinct in sound from fifty.
items.cn: 现代英语拼写定为 fifteen，发音与 fifty 明确区分。

items.en: Sports such as rugby and tennis gave the word team meanings.
items.cn: 橄榄球与网球等运动赋予该词团队义。

note.en: Look-alikes share the five root or the teen ending; near-meaning words sit among numbers.

intro.en: Fifty is the Germanic compound five-plus-ten at the tens level: five tens, spoken as one word since Old English.

senses.title: To use physical force

senses.exampleCN: 男孩们在校园里打了起来。
senses.why: Bodies first: the word begins with fists and muscle.
senses.whyCN: 身体为先：这个词始于拳头与肌肉。

senses.title: To take part in a war or battle
senses.definition: to take part in armed conflict as a soldier or group
senses.definitionCN: 作为士兵或团体参加武装冲突
senses.example: They fought bravely to defend the city.

senses.whyCN: 一对一的力量放大后便是军队与战争。

senses.title: To struggle against something bad
senses.definition: to try hard to stop or defeat something harmful

senses.title: To compete hard for something

senses.title: To quarrel or argue

senses.why: Words replace fists, but the force behind them stays the same.

intro.en: Fight is a Germanic strong verb whose old past tense fought survives intact, from a root that once meant to plait or tie a rope — force binding into struggle.
intro.cn: fight 是日耳曼强变化动词，古过去式 fought 完整保留；词根原义或为「编结、捆扎」，引申为缠斗。

items.en: A reconstructed root fekhtan meant 'to plait, twist together', which grew into fighting and fencing words.
items.cn: 一般认为，重构词根 fekhtan 意为「编结、绞缠」，衍生出搏斗与剑术一类词。

items.en: Old English feohtan meant 'to fight, contend', with past tense feaht.
items.cn: 古英语 feohtan 意为「搏斗、争斗」，过去式为 feaht。

items.en: Middle English fighten kept the strong past, spelled fought.
items.cn: 中古英语 fighten 保留强变化过去式，拼作 fought。

items.en: The noun fight grew beside the verb for battles, quarrels and struggles.
items.cn: 现代英语在动词旁发展出名词 fight，兼指战斗、争执与抗争。

items.en: Metaphors spread widely: fighting fit, a fight for survival, fighter jets.
items.cn: 比喻广泛传播：fighting fit、a fight for survival、fighter jets。

note.en: Look-alikes share the fi- shape or the old root; near-meaning words cover combat and struggle.
note.cn: 形近组共享 fi- 字形或古老词根；近义组覆盖搏斗与抗争。

sceneCN: 这里 figure 是动词，指「想出、弄明白」，对应第 6 个义项；句意为她加班到很晚，弄清总数错在哪里。

pos.zh: 数字；图表；人物；身材；轮廓

成形； figurative art

senses.title: A number, especially in records
senses.definition: a number, especially one shown in statistics or accounts
senses.definitionCN: 数字，尤指统计或账目中的数值
senses.example: The sales figures surprised everyone.
senses.exampleCN: 销售数字令所有人大吃一惊。
senses.why: Written marks that carry quantity are figures: the ink itself shows shape.
senses.whyCN: 承载数量的书写符号即 figures：墨迹本身就显示形状。

senses.title: The shape of a body
senses.definition: the shape of a person's body
senses.definitionCN: 人身体的形状
senses.example: She keeps her figure by swimming.
senses.exampleCN: 她靠游泳保持身材。
senses.why: The outer form of a person is the shape their life is drawn in.
senses.whyCN: 人的外形是生命被勾画出的轮廓。

senses.title: A person seen as a shape or name
senses.definition: a person, especially one important or well known
senses.definitionCN: 一个人，尤指重要或知名的人
senses.example: He became a key figure in the reform.
senses.exampleCN: 他成了改革中的关键人物。
senses.why: From afar, people are shapes moving in history: figures on a stage.
senses.whyCN: 远观时，人是历史中移动的剪影：舞台上的 figure。

senses.title: A diagram or drawing
senses.definition: a drawing or diagram in a book to explain something
senses.definitionCN: 书中用于说明事物的图示
senses.example: See figure 3 for the wiring diagram.
senses.exampleCN: 接线图见图 3。
senses.why: A picture fixed the meaning before words could: figure as diagram.
senses.whyCN: 在言语之前，图画先固定了含义：figure 即图示。

senses.title: To calculate a number
senses.definition: to work out an amount with numbers
senses.definitionCN: 用数字算出一个金额或数量
senses.example: We figured the cost at two thousand.
senses.exampleCN: 我们估算成本为两千。
senses.why: Moving shapes and numbers about in the mind is how arithmetic feels.
senses.whyCN: 在脑中搬运数字与形状，正是算术的体验。

senses.title: To understand after thinking
senses.definition: to understand or find an answer by thinking
senses.definitionCN: 通过思考理解或找到答案
senses.example: He figured out why the engine stalled.
senses.exampleCN: 他弄明白了引擎熄火的原因。
senses.why: Give the shapes time to settle and the answer takes form.
senses.whyCN: 让那些形状在脑中沉淀，答案便成形。

intro.en: Figure comes from Latin figura 'shape, form', from fingere 'to shape', and keeps both the drawn outline and the formed idea.
intro.cn: figure 源自拉丁语 figura「形状、形态」，出自 fingere「塑造」，同时保留「勾画的轮廓」与「成形的观念」。

items.en: Fingere meant 'to shape, mould'; its noun figura meant 'a shape or form'.
items.cn: fingere 意为「塑造、模制」；其名词 figura 意为「形状、形态」。

items.en: Old French figure carried the shape sense into Romance speech.
items.cn: 古法语 figure 把形状义带入罗曼语。

items.en: Middle English borrowed figure for body form, diagrams and numerals.
items.cn: 中古英语借入 figure，指体形、图示与数字。

items.en: The verb grew: to figure meant to calculate, then to reason out.
items.cn: 现代英语发展出动词义：先表计算，后表推理明白。

items.en: Figure out became the everyday phrase for solving problems.
items.cn: figure out 成为日常表达「解决问题」的固定说法。

note.en: Look-alikes share the fig- shape; near-meaning words cover shapes, numbers and understanding.
note.cn: 形近组共享 fig- 字形；近义组覆盖形状、数字与理解。

entries.definition: the Latin verb 'to shape' behind figure
entries.definitionCN: figure 背后的拉丁动词「塑造」

entries.definition: a small ornamental figure
thread-like structure; close shape but different root
a count or amount
the outline of a thing
to grasp the meaning fully

normalIntro.en: Five handles from the shape root and daily phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 五个来自形状词根与日常短语的记忆抓手。

normal.en: figure out is the phrase you need for solving problems.
normal.cn: figure out 是解决问题必用的短语。

normal.en: a figure can be a number, a person, or a body shape: all are forms.
normal.cn: figure 可以是数字、人物或身材：都是「形」。

normal.en: keeping your figure keeps your shape.
normal.cn: keep one's figure 就是保持身材。

normal.en: public figure is a person in the public eye.
normal.cn: public figure 指公众人物。

normal.en: figure skating draws shapes on the ice.
normal.cn: figure skating 在冰上勾画图形。

abstract.en: A figure is a thought that has learned to hold its shape.
abstract.cn: figure 是学会了保持形状的念头。

abstract.en: Numbers are shapes we count with.
abstract.cn: 数字是我们用来计数的形状。

abstract.en: To figure out is to trace the outline of an answer.
abstract.cn: figure out 就是描出答案的轮廓。

examples.en: Check the figures before the report goes out.
examples.cn: 报告发出前先核对数字。

examples.en: We finally figured out how the system works.
examples.cn: 我们终于弄清楚了系统的运作方式。

examples.en: A tall figure stood at the end of the pier.
examples.cn: 码头尽头立着一个高高的身影。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「非够」—— 数字必须核对，非够不可 → figure 数字；figure out 想明白

root: 源自拉丁语 figura「形状」，出自 fingere「塑造」（与 fiction「虚构」同根），经古法语 figure 进入英语；核心是「被塑出之形」。

sensesIntro.en: From written numbers outward to body shape, notable people, diagrams, calculating and understanding.
sensesIntro.cn: 从书写数字扩展到体形、知名人物、图示、计算与想明白。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an outline that can be drawn, counted or recognized.
core.cn: 核心意象：可被描画、计数或辨认的轮廓。

branches.en: THE MARKS: numbers on a page.
THE BODY: a human outline.
THE PERSON: a notable name.
THE CALCULUS: diagrams and arithmetic.
THE ANSWER: understanding that takes form.

intro.en: The fingere family is rich: figure, fiction and their relatives all shape meaning.
intro.cn: fingere 词族庞大：figure、fiction 及亲属词都在「塑形」。

latinIntro.en: Latin fingere 'to shape, devise' produces both the shapes we see and the stories we tell.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 fingere「塑造、构想」同时产生可见之形与所讲之故事。
