A porcelain figurine sat on the shelf.

items.meaning: to spoil the shape or looks
a person in the public eye
items.example: The mayor is a public figure.

items.meaning: a leader with no real power
items.example: The king was a mere figurehead.

definition_zh: 装满；填满；充满；填补（空缺）；填充物；饱
definition_en: to put enough of something into a space until it is full, or to take a job or role; also the material used to fill
core_image: 水壶被一股水流缓缓注满，水面最终齐了壶口
scene: 加油站里，司机拧开油箱盖准备加满油。Please fill the tank with regular petrol.
sceneCN: 这里 fill 是动词，指「把容器装满」，对应第 1 个义项；句意为请给油箱加满普通汽油。

derivatives.zh: 馅料；补牙材料；填充（fill 的动名词，指被填之物）
填充物；补白（fill 加施动者后缀 -er，指用于填充之物）
履行；实现（fill 的同族变体，指完全填满义务或期望）

senses.title: To make a container full
senses.definition: to put as much as possible into a container or space
senses.definitionCN: 把容器或空间装到最满
senses.example: She filled the kettle with water.
senses.exampleCN: 她把水壶装满水。
senses.why: Pouring in until the brim is reached is the picture the word was born from.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的画面就是一直倒入直至齐口。

senses.title: To occupy a space or time
senses.definition: to spread through a space or period
senses.definitionCN: 弥漫于空间或时段之中
senses.example: Music filled the hall.
senses.exampleCN: 音乐充满了大厅。
senses.why: What pours in can be sound or smoke: space is a container too.
senses.whyCN: 涌入的可以是声音或烟雾：空间本身就是容器。

senses.title: To take a job or role
senses.definition: to take or occupy a job, position or need
senses.definitionCN: 承担职位或满足需求
senses.example: Two new teachers filled the vacancies.
senses.exampleCN: 两位新教师填补了空缺。
senses.why: A vacancy is a hole in the roster, and holes ask to be filled.
senses.whyCN: 空缺是名单上的洞，洞等待被填。

senses.title: To complete a form or order
senses.definition: to write in the parts of a form, or to supply what an order asks
senses.definitionCN: 在表格中写入内容，或按订单供货
senses.example: Please fill in your name and address.
senses.exampleCN: 请填写姓名与地址。
senses.why: An empty form is a waiting container for ink and facts.
senses.whyCN: 空表格是等待墨水与事实的容器。

senses.title: Food that satisfies hunger
senses.definition: food that makes you feel full
senses.definitionCN: 令人产生饱感的食物
senses.example: Porridge is cheap and filling.
senses.exampleCN: 粥便宜又顶饱。
senses.why: The stomach is a container, and fill works on it like any other.
senses.whyCN: 胃也是容器，fill 对它一视同仁。

intro.en: Fill is a Germanic word of the full family: the adjective full turned into the verb of making full.
intro.cn: fill 属日耳曼语「满」家族：形容词 full 转化为「使满」的动词。

items.en: A reconstructed root ful- meant 'full'; the verb stem fulljan meant 'to make full'.
items.cn: 一般认为，重构词根 ful- 意为「满」；动词词干 fulljan 意为「使满」。

items.en: Old English fyllan meant 'to fill, complete', a causative of full.
items.cn: 古英语 fyllan 意为「装满、完成」，是 full 的使动形式。

items.en: Middle English fillen kept the causative sense for containers and roles alike.
items.cn: 中古英语 fillen 的使动义兼指容器与职位。

items.en: Phrasal verbs filled in, filled up and filled out spread the idea to forms and shapes.
items.cn: 现代英语短语 fill in、fill up、fill out 把概念扩展到表格与体形。

items.en: The noun grew for dental fillings, pie fillings and fuel fills.
items.cn: 名词义扩展到补牙材料、馅料与加油量。

note.en: Look-alikes share the full root or close spelling; near-meaning words occupy the space of fullness.
note.cn: 形近组共享 full 词根或相近拼写；近义组处于「满」的义场。

entries.definition: containing as much as possible; the adjective behind the verb
entries.definitionCN: 满的；动词背后的形容词

entries.definition: to carry out or complete
entries.definitionCN: 履行；实现；同族强化的「满」

entries.definition: a raised piece of land; one letter apart and unrelated
entries.definitionCN: 小山；仅一字母之差而词源无关

entries.definition: to put goods or cargo into
to push material into a space
to be full to the very edge

normalIntro.en: Five handles from the full family and phrasal verbs.
normalIntro.cn: 五个来自 full 词族与短语的记忆抓手。

normal.en: fill and full are the same family: to fill is to make full.
normal.cn: fill 与 full 同族：fill 就是使 full。

normal.en: fill in a form writes into the empty lines.
normal.cn: fill in a form 即在空行里填写。

normal.en: fill up the tank takes it to the very top.
normal.cn: fill up the tank 把油加到顶。

normal.en: a filling meal fills the stomach.
normal.cn: filling meal 就是吃饱的一餐。

normal.en: fulfil goes further: it fills an expectation completely.
normal.cn: fulfil 更进一步：把期望填满。

abstract.en: Every empty thing is a question; to fill is to answer it.
abstract.cn: 凡空缺皆提问；fill 就是作答。

abstract.en: Joy poured in fills a life to the brim.
abstract.cn: 倾注的喜悦把生命盛到齐口。

abstract.en: Time is a jug: some days fill slowly, some spill fast.
abstract.cn: 时间是一只壶：有的日子慢慢盛满，有的匆匆溢出。

examples.en: Fill the bucket halfway before you start.
examples.cn: 开始前先把桶装到一半。

examples.en: Her kindness filled the whole office with warmth.
examples.cn: 她的善意让整个办公室充满暖意。

examples.en: The dentist replaced the old filling in my tooth.
examples.cn: 牙医更换了我牙上的旧填充物。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「肥哦」—— 倒满一壶肥厚的浓汤 → fill 装满

root: 出自古英语 fyllan「使满」，是 full「满」的使动形式，上溯日耳曼词根 ful-；核心是「把空处填到齐口」。

sensesIntro.en: From pouring into containers outward to occupying space, filling jobs, forms and stomachs.
sensesIntro.cn: 从往容器倾倒，扩展到充满空间、填补职位、填写表格与填饱肚子。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: liquid rising in a vessel until it meets the brim.
core.cn: 核心意象：液体在容器中升起，直至与杯口齐平。

branches.en: THE VESSEL: filling containers.
THE SPACE: sound and light that fill rooms.
branches.cn: 空间：充满房间的声与光。

branches.en: THE ROLE: vacancies that take people.
THE FORM: lines that wait for ink.
THE STOMACH: food that satisfies.

intro.en: The full family stretches from fill to fulfil and festive plenty.
intro.cn: full 词族从 fill 延伸到 fulfil 与丰盛一族。

latinIntro.en: Latin used plenus 'full', giving plenty and plenty-family words, unrelated to the Germanic line.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语用 plenus「满」，派生出 plenty 一族，与日耳曼语支无关。

items.example: The magazine used a filler photo.
items.exampleCN: 杂志用了一张补白照片。

items.meaning: to write into blanks; to substitute
to complete a form; to grow plumper

items.example: The filling station closed at ten.

definition_zh: 找到；发现；查明；发觉；发现物；判定
definition_en: to discover something you are looking for, or to notice something by chance; also something discovered or a court decision
core_image: 手电光扫过草丛，忽然停在一枚失而复得的钥匙上
scene: 搬家清理时，一只旧木箱从床底被拖了出来。We found a box of old letters behind the wardrobe.
sceneCN: 这里 find 是动词，指「偶然发现」，对应第 2 个义项；句意为我们在衣柜后发现一盒旧信。

pos.zh: 找到；发现；查明；发觉；判定

derivatives.zh: 调查结果；发现（find 的动名词，指研究所得结论）
发现者；取景器（find 加施动者后缀 -er，指找到之人或装置）
调查结果（finding 的复数，指一系列结论）

senses.title: To discover something sought
senses.definition: to discover something you have been looking for
senses.definitionCN: 找到一直在寻找的东西
senses.example: At last she found her keys.
senses.exampleCN: 她终于找到了钥匙。
senses.why: Search ends in contact: eyes, hands and the sought thing meet.
senses.whyCN: 搜寻止于接触：目光、双手与目标相遇。

senses.title: To come across by chance
senses.definition: to notice or come across something unexpectedly
senses.definitionCN: 出乎意料地注意到某物
senses.example: We found a coin in the garden.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在花园里发现一枚硬币。
senses.why: Finding is not always planned: the world offers surprises.
senses.whyCN: 发现不必经过计划：世界自带惊喜。

senses.title: To learn a fact
senses.definition: to discover a fact after inquiry
senses.definitionCN: 经查问而得知事实
senses.example: Please find out when the train leaves.
senses.exampleCN: 请查清楚火车几点开。
senses.why: Facts hide too; inquiry is a search of another kind.
senses.whyCN: 事实也会藏匿；查问是另一种搜寻。

senses.title: To feel or judge something
senses.definition: to experience or judge something in a stated way
senses.definitionCN: 以某种方式体验或评判某事
senses.example: I find this book fascinating.
senses.exampleCN: 我觉得这本书引人入胜。
senses.why: Opinions are found the way objects are: by looking closely.
senses.whyCN: 看法与物件一样需要寻找：靠仔细观察得出。

senses.title: A valuable discovery
senses.definition: something good or valuable that is discovered
senses.definitionCN: 被发现的好东西或有价值之物
senses.example: That little bookshop is a real find.
senses.exampleCN: 那家小书店真是难得的发现。
senses.why: The verb hardens into a noun: the found thing itself.
senses.whyCN: 动词凝固为名词：被找到之物本身。

intro.en: Find is an ancient Germanic strong verb, once meaning simply 'to come upon', whose past tense found also gave found, 'to establish'.
intro.cn: find 是古老的日耳曼强变化动词，本义「遇上」，其过去式 found 同时催生了 found「创立」。

items.en: A reconstructed root finthan meant 'to come upon'; Gothic and Old Norse show close cousins.
items.cn: 一般认为，重构词根 finthan 意为「遇上」；哥特语与古诺斯语中有近亲。

items.en: Old English findan meant 'to meet with, discover', with past funde.
items.cn: 古英语 findan 意为「遇见、发现」，过去式为 funde。

items.en: Middle English finden kept the strong past found, and the noun find appeared.
items.cn: 中古英语 finden 保留强变化过去式 found，并出现名词 find。

items.en: Find out spread the sense to facts and information.
items.cn: 现代英语 find out 把词义扩展到事实与信息。

items.en: The same past stem found gave the verb found, 'to establish', a true sibling.
items.cn: 同一过去式词干 found 又派生出 found「创立」，构成真正的兄弟词。

note.en: Look-alikes share the find spelling or the found stem; near-meaning words cover discovery.
note.cn: 形近组共享 find 拼写或 found 词干；近义组覆盖发现义场。

entries.definition: the past of find, and also the verb 'to establish'
entries.definitionCN: find 的过去式，也是动词「创立」

normal.en: find out is the everyday way to say investigate.
normal.cn: find out 是日常表达「查明」的方式。

normal.en: found the past also founded a city: same stem, two verbs.
normal.cn: 过去式 found 同时创立了一座城：同一词干，两个动词。

normal.en: a great find is a discovery worth telling friends about.
normal.cn: a great find 是值得向朋友炫耀的发现。

normal.en: find fault with means to complain about small things.
normal.cn: find fault with 表示吹毛求疵。

abstract.en: To find is to end a search the world started.
abstract.cn: find 是为世界开启的搜寻画上句点。

abstract.en: Some truths find you before you find them.
abstract.cn: 有些真相会先于你找到它们。

abstract.en: Discovery is contact: distance closes and the object is yours.
abstract.cn: 发现即接触：距离闭合，物归于你。

examples.en: The police found the missing child in the park.
examples.cn: 警方在公园里找到了失踪的孩子。

examples.en: Scientists found traces of water in the rock samples.
examples.cn: 科学家在岩石样本中发现了水的痕迹。

examples.en: I find it easier to write in the morning.
examples.cn: 我觉得早晨写作更容易。

definition_zh: 好的；优质的；晴朗的；纤细的；罚款；处以罚款
definition_en: of high quality, thin or delicate, clear and bright, or satisfactory; as a noun and verb, a sum paid as punishment
core_image: 一根细线在阳光下亮得几乎透明，品质与纤细合为一体
scene: 天气预报刚结束，阳光下孩子们的球赛已经开场。The morning was fine, so the match went ahead.
sceneCN: 这里 fine 是形容词，指「晴朗的」，对应第 3 个义项；句意为早晨天气晴好，比赛如期进行。

pos.zh: 好的；优质的；晴朗的；纤细的

derivatives.zh: 精细地； finely chopped

senses.title: Of high quality
senses.definition: of very good quality or skill
senses.definitionCN: 质量或技艺极佳的
senses.example: The museum holds a fine collection of jade.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆收藏了精美的玉器。
senses.why: What is rare and well made earns praise: quality is the root of the word.
senses.whyCN: 稀少而精良之物值得称赞：品质是这个词的根。

senses.title: Thin and delicate
senses.definition: very thin or in very small pieces
senses.definitionCN: 极细的或被切得极小的
senses.example: The brush drew a fine line.
senses.exampleCN: 画笔勾勒出一条细线。
senses.why: Thin is precious in craft: the finer the line, the finer the hand.
senses.whyCN: 工艺以细为贵：线条越细，手上功夫越精。

senses.title: Clear and cloudless
senses.definition: bright and without rain or clouds
senses.definitionCN: 明亮而无雨无云的
senses.example: We chose a fine day for the picnic.
senses.exampleCN: 我们挑了个晴天去野餐。
senses.why: Weather without cloud is weather of quality: the same root praises it.
senses.whyCN: 无云的天气就是好天气：同一词根表达赞美。

senses.title: Satisfactory; well
senses.definition: in a good or acceptable state
senses.definitionCN: 处于良好或可接受的状态
senses.example: Everything is fine now.
senses.exampleCN: 现在一切都好了。
senses.why: Acceptable is a soft form of excellent: good enough to pass.
senses.whyCN: 「可以」是「极好」的柔化版本：好到足以过关。

senses.title: Money paid as punishment
senses.definition: a sum of money paid as a penalty
senses.definitionCN: 作为惩罚而缴付的款项
senses.example: He paid a fine for parking.
senses.exampleCN: 他因乱停车缴了罚款。
senses.why: Money settles the score the fist once did: an ending priced in cash.
senses.whyCN: 金钱接替拳头来了结恩怨：一次用现金定价的了结。

intro.en: Fine comes from Latin finis 'an end', for a settled payment, and via Old French for a finished, refined quality.
intro.cn: fine 源自拉丁语 finis「终结」，一脉指已定结的罚金，经古法语另一脉指精炼完备的品质。

items.en: Finis meant 'end, boundary', the root also of final and finish.
items.cn: finis 意为「终结、边界」，也是 final 与 finish 的词根。

items.en: Medieval Latin finis took the sense of 'a payment that settles a dispute'.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 finis 衍生出「了结争端的款项」义。

items.en: Old French fin meant both 'settled payment' and 'of refined quality'.
items.cn: 古法语 fin 兼指「已定的款项」与「精炼的品质」。

items.en: Middle English borrowed fine in both directions, quality and penalty.
items.cn: 中古英语沿两条路径借入 fine：品质与罚金。

items.en: Modern English keeps the adjective rich — fine weather, fine silk — and the fine of law.
items.cn: 现代英语保留丰富的形容词义与法律上的罚款义。

note.en: Look-alikes share the fin- root or close spelling; near-meaning words cover quality and thinness.
note.cn: 形近组共享 fin- 词根或相近拼写；近义组覆盖品质与纤细。

normal.en: fine, final, finish all come from finis, 'end': quality is the end of effort.
normal.cn: fine、final、finish 皆出自 finis「终结」：品质是努力的终点。

normal.en: a fine day is weather at its best.
normal.cn: a fine day 是天气的最好状态。

normal.en: fine sand is sand cut to its thinnest.
normal.cn: fine sand 是被磨到最细的沙。

normal.en: pay the fine settles the debt at the end of a case.
normal.cn: 缴罚款是在案件终点结清债务。

normal.en: Fine, thanks is the polite answer to How are you.
normal.cn: Fine, thanks 是回答 How are you 的客套语。

abstract.en: Quality is an edge reached: the fine is where effort ends.
abstract.cn: 品质是抵达的边缘：fine 即努力的终点。

abstract.en: A thin line is a decision drawn in silk.
abstract.cn: 细线是以丝线画下的决断。

abstract.en: A fine is a debt with a date: the end written in money.
abstract.cn: 罚款是带日期的债：以金钱写就的终点。

examples.en: The tailor used fine wool for the winter coat.
examples.cn: 裁缝用上等细羊毛做冬衣。

examples.en: The driver was fined for speeding on the motorway.
examples.cn: 司机因在高速上超速被罚款。

examples.en: Everything turned out fine in the end.
examples.cn: 最终一切顺利。

sensesIntro.en: From settled endings outward to quality, thinness, clear weather, satisfaction and the penalty.

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line drawn to its finest end.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条被画到最细末端的线。

Confine the topic to one page.

definition_zh: 完成；结束；用完；终结；结尾；表面处理
definition_en: to bring something to an end, or to come to the last part; also the end itself or the surface quality of an object
core_image: 长跑道上最后一条白线，冲过它一切宣告完成
scene: 装修队给新桌子打上最后一层清漆，大家直起腰来。The varnish gives the table a smooth, glossy finish.
sceneCN: 这里 finish 是名词，指「表面处理效果」，对应第 6 个义项；句意为清漆让桌面光滑发亮。

senses.title: To bring to an end
senses.definition: to complete something or bring it to its final point
senses.definitionCN: 完成某事或使之到达终点
senses.example: She finished the report last night.
senses.exampleCN: 她昨晚完成了报告。
senses.why: The end is a boundary you choose to cross, and the word marks the crossing.
senses.whyCN: 终点是你选择跨过的边界，这个词标记的正是跨越本身。

senses.title: To use up completely
senses.definition: to use or eat all of something
senses.definitionCN: 把某物全部用掉或吃掉
senses.example: The kids finished the cake in minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们几分钟就吃完了蛋糕。
senses.why: A supply that reaches zero has also met its end.
senses.whyCN: 用尽的供给同样抵达了它的终点。

senses.title: The end or last part
senses.definition: the last part of something
senses.definitionCN: 某事物的最后一部分
senses.example: The story has a surprising finish.
senses.exampleCN: 故事的结尾出人意料。
senses.why: Where things stop has its own name.
senses.whyCN: 事物停驻之处自有其名。

senses.title: The place where a race ends
senses.definition: the point where a race or journey ends
senses.definitionCN: 比赛或旅程的终点处
senses.example: Two runners crossed the finish together.
senses.exampleCN: 两名选手同时冲过终点。
senses.why: The line on the track is the end made visible.
senses.whyCN: 赛道上的白线是可见的终点。

senses.title: The surface quality of an object
senses.definition: the appearance or texture of a surface after treatment
senses.definitionCN: 处理过后表面的外观或质感
senses.example: The desk has a satin finish.
senses.exampleCN: 书桌呈缎面光泽。
senses.why: The last coat decides how the whole surface feels: an end you can touch.
senses.whyCN: 最后一道工序决定表面触感：可以摸到的终点。

senses.title: To make someone exhausted
senses.definition: to make someone completely tired
senses.definitionCN: 令人彻底精疲力竭
senses.example: That climb finished me.
senses.exampleCN: 那次攀爬把我累垮了。
senses.why: What ends a person's strength is also a finish.
senses.whyCN: 耗尽气力之事也是一种终结。

items.cn: finire 意为「限定、终结」，建立在 finis「边界、终结」之上。

items.cn: 古法语 finir 表示使事物到达终点。

items.en: Middle English finishen covered both completing work and ending life's chapters.
items.cn: 中古英语 finishen 兼指完成工作与终结篇章。

items.en: The noun grew: the finish of a race, the finish of a surface.
items.cn: 现代英语名词义扩展：赛跑的终点、器物的饰面。

normal.en: be finished with means you are done and can move on.

normal.en: the finish line is where all effort ends.

normal.en: finish up means to complete the last small part.

abstract.en: Every finish is a door: behind it, a next task waits.
abstract.cn: 每个终点都是一扇门：门后还有下一件事。

abstract.en: To finish is to give a thing its boundary.

abstract.en: A polish is an ending you can feel with your hand.

examples.en: The marathon runner finished just before dark.

definition_en: burning with flames and light, a burning that destroys, the heat of a hearth, or gunshots; as verbs, to shoot, dismiss or set alight

scene: 冬夜的山屋里，柴火噼啪作响映红了围坐者的脸。We sat around the fire and told stories till midnight.

senses.title: Burning with flames
senses.definition: the state of burning that produces light and heat
senses.definitionCN: 产生光与热的燃烧状态
senses.example: The hut went up in flames when a fire started in the kitchen.
senses.exampleCN: 厨房起火，小屋被火焰吞噬。
senses.why: Light, heat and eating wood: the first picture of fire is consumption made visible.
senses.whyCN: 光、热与吞食木柴：火焰最初的画面即「可见的吞噬」。

senses.title: A destructive burning
senses.definition: an uncontrolled burning that destroys property
senses.definitionCN: 失去控制、摧毁财物的燃烧
senses.example: The factory fire destroyed three workshops.
senses.exampleCN: 工厂火灾烧毁了三间车间。
senses.why: When fire escapes its hearth it turns from servant to enemy.
senses.whyCN: 火焰一旦脱离炉膛，便从仆从变为敌人。

senses.title: A hearth or campfire
senses.definition: a controlled fire used for warmth, cooking or ceremony
senses.definitionCN: 用于取暖、做饭或仪式的受控之火
senses.example: They cooked supper over an open fire.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在篝火上做晚饭。
senses.why: Tamed fire gathers people around it: warmth is social.
senses.whyCN: 被驯服的火把人聚拢：温暖具有社交性。

senses.title: Gunshots
senses.definition: the shots fired from guns
senses.definitionCN: 枪炮射出的弹药
senses.example: The soldiers came under heavy fire.
senses.exampleCN: 士兵们遭到猛烈炮火袭击。
senses.why: Guns eject fire, so the discharge of weapons borrows the flame.
senses.whyCN: 枪炮喷吐火焰，于是武器的发射借用了火之名。

senses.title: Strong emotion or energy
senses.definition: intense emotion, energy or inspiration
senses.definitionCN: 强烈的情绪、干劲或灵感
senses.example: Her speech was full of fire.
senses.exampleCN: 她的演讲充满激情。
senses.why: Burning inside the body is indistinguishable from burning in the mind.
senses.whyCN: 体内之烧与心中之烧在语言上难分彼此。

senses.title: To dismiss from a job
senses.definition: to make someone leave their job
senses.definitionCN: 使某人离开工作岗位
senses.example: He was fired for missing deadlines.
senses.exampleCN: 他因屡屡误期被解雇。
senses.why: The old way of ending work was a payment: firing was settling the account.
senses.whyCN: 旧时终止雇佣的方式是结清款项：解雇即结账。

intro.en: Fire is a native Germanic word of the hearth and the flame, older than writing, with cousins across the Germanic languages.
intro.cn: fire 是属于炉膛与火焰的日耳曼本族词，比文字更古老，在各日耳曼语言中都有同族词。

items.en: A reconstructed root fur- meant 'fire'; German Feuer and Dutch vuur are cousins.

items.en: Guns made fire the word for gunfire and for shooting.

normal.en: catch fire means flames have begun.
normal.cn: catch fire 表示火已烧起来。

normal.en: fire a gun and fire an employee share one verb: both are sudden endings.
normal.cn: fire a gun 与 fire an employee 共用一动词：都是突然的终结。

normal.en: German Feuer is the same word: the hearth family is old.
normal.cn: 德语 Feuer 与之同词：炉火词族古老。

normal.en: full of fire means burning with energy.
normal.cn: full of fire 表示充满干劲。

normal.en: open fire means to start shooting.
normal.cn: open fire 表示开始射击。

abstract.en: Fire is energy that has found a body to wear.
abstract.cn: 火是找到了躯壳的能量。

abstract.en: Anger is a house fire of the mind: it starts small and spreads.
abstract.cn: 愤怒是心灵的家宅之火：起于微末，蔓延成灾。

abstract.en: Dismissal is a door that burns on the way out.
abstract.cn: 解雇是一扇离开时还在燃烧的门。

examples.en: Smoke poured from the burning building before the fire brigade arrived.
examples.cn: 消防队赶到前，浓烟已从起火大楼涌出。

examples.en: The company fired three managers last month.
examples.cn: 公司上个月解雇了三名经理。

examples.en: The crowd was fired up by the band's last song.
examples.cn: 乐队的最后一首歌点燃了全场观众的热情。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「法爷」—— 火苗乱窜，法爷喊一声「法爷水来也」→ fire 火

root: 日耳曼本族词，出自古英语 fyr「火」，上溯重构词根 fur-；德语 Feuer、荷兰语 vuur 同族；核心是「燃烧之光与热」。

sensesIntro.en: From the flame outward to disasters, hearths, gunfire, passion and dismissal.
sensesIntro.cn: 从火焰出发，扩展到火灾、炉火、炮火、激情与解雇。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: orange flames that light the dark and eat their fuel.
core.cn: 核心意象：照亮黑暗并吞噬燃料的橙色火焰。

branches.en: THE FLAME: burning itself.
THE DISASTER: fire out of control.
THE HEARTH: fire tamed for warmth.
THE GUNFIRE: weapons that spit flame.
THE BURN WITHIN: passion, and the job that ends.
branches.cn: 内在之烧：激情，与被终止的职位。

intro.en: Fire compounds eagerly: firefighter, fireplace, firearm and more.
intro.cn: fire 极易复合构词：firefighter、fireplace、firearm 等。

latinIntro.en: Latin used ignis 'fire', root of ignite, unrelated to the Germanic fire.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语用 ignis「火」（ignite 的词根），与日耳曼的 fire 无关。

items.example: The bricks were fired at noon.
The school held a fire drill.

definition_zh: 第一的；最初的；首要的；首先；第一次；第一名
definition_en: coming before all others in order, time or importance; the earliest instance or the winning position
core_image: 颁奖台上最高的那一格，站上去的人身后全是来路
scene: 清晨的赛道上，观众屏息等待第一位冲线者。She was the first to cross the finish line.
sceneCN: 这里 first 是形容词，指「第一的」，对应第 1 个义项；句意为她是第一个冲过终点线的人。

pos.zh: 第一的；最初的；最重要的

derivatives.zh: 首先（第一点）（first 加副词后缀 -ly，用于列举）
头生的；长子（first 与 born 复合，指最先出生者）
最重要的（fore 与 most 复合，同族词，指居首位的）

senses.title: Before all others in order
senses.definition: coming before every other one in a series
senses.definitionCN: 在序列中先于其他一切
senses.example: This is my first visit to Paris.
senses.exampleCN: 这是我第一次来巴黎。
senses.why: Order begins somewhere, and the word marks the starting point.
senses.whyCN: 次序总有个起点，这个词标记的就是起点。

senses.title: Earliest in time
senses.definition: happening or existing before anything else
senses.definitionCN: 先于其他一切而发生或存在的
senses.example: The first trains ran before the railway was finished.
senses.exampleCN: 首批火车在铁路完工前就已运行。
senses.why: Time also lines up: the earliest is the first.
senses.whyCN: 时间同样成列：最早者即第一。

senses.title: Most important
senses.definition: more important than anything else
senses.definitionCN: 比其他一切都重要
senses.example: Safety comes first in this lab.
senses.exampleCN: 在这间实验室安全第一。
senses.why: Ranking by value reuses the line: the top of the list is first.
senses.whyCN: 按价值排序重复使用这条线：清单顶端即第一。

senses.title: Before anything else; firstly
senses.definition: before doing anything else
senses.definitionCN: 在做其他任何事之前
senses.example: First, wash your hands.
senses.exampleCN: 首先，洗手。
senses.why: Instructions start at the front of the line too.
senses.whyCN: 指令同样从队伍最前端开始。

senses.title: The winning position
senses.definition: the position of the winner in a race or contest
senses.definitionCN: 比赛或竞赛中获胜者的位置
senses.example: He took first in the maths contest.
senses.exampleCN: 他在数学竞赛中得了第一名。
senses.why: The fastest reaches the end before all: winning is being first.
senses.whyCN: 最快者先于所有人抵达终点：夺冠即是第一。

intro.en: First is the superlative of an old word for 'before': fore, compare, whose superlative froze into an adjective of its own.
intro.cn: first 是古老词「在前」（fore）的最高级形式：这一最高级凝固成了独立的形容词。

items.en: A reconstructed root fur- meant 'forward, before', the same stock as fore.
items.cn: 一般认为，重构词根 fur- 意为「向前、在前」，与 fore 同源。

items.en: Old English fyrest meant 'foremost, earliest', the superlative of fore.
items.cn: 古英语 fyrest 意为「最前的、最早的」，是 fore 的最高级。

items.en: Middle English first kept both the order sense and the importance sense.
items.cn: 中古英语 first 兼指次序与重要性。

items.en: First settled as the standard ordinal of one, against second's Latin origin.
items.cn: 现代英语中 first 成为 one 的标准序数词，而 second 出自拉丁语。

items.en: Fixed phrases like first aid and first-hand spread widely.
items.cn: first aid 与 first-hand 等固定短语广泛传播。

note.en: Look-alikes share the fore root or close spelling; near-meaning words head the same line.
note.cn: 形近组共享 fore 词根或相近拼写；近义组同在队列最前。

entries.definition: a closed hand; letters rearranged, meaning far away
entries.definitionCN: 拳头；字母换位而意义相远

entries.definition: the most important; a superlative cousin
entries.definitionCN: 最重要的；最高级同族词

entries.definition: to break open suddenly; sound-close but unrelated
happening at the beginning
most important or earliest
in the top position

normalIntro.en: Five handles from the fore root and fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 五个来自 fore 词根与固定短语的记忆抓手。

normal.en: first is the superlative of fore: the one before all others.
normal.cn: first 是 fore 的最高级：先于其他一切者。

normal.en: first of all opens any list of instructions.
normal.cn: first of all 用于开启任何指令清单。

normal.en: at first means in the beginning, before things changed.
normal.cn: at first 表示起初，在变化发生之前。

normal.en: first aid is the help given before doctors arrive.
normal.cn: first aid 是医生到来之前的救助。

normal.en: second is the odd one out: it comes from Latin, first from Germanic.
normal.cn: second 有点另类：它出自拉丁语，first 出自日耳曼语。

abstract.en: Every first is a door the second walks through.
abstract.cn: 每个「第一」都是「第二」要穿过的门。

abstract.en: Beginnings are remembered longest.
abstract.cn: 开端被记得最久。

abstract.en: The podium's top step is just the front of a queue.
abstract.cn: 领奖台最高一级不过是队伍的最前端。

examples.en: First read the questions, then listen to the tape.
examples.cn: 先读题，然后听录音。

examples.en: Her first novel won a national prize.
examples.cn: 她的处女作获得了一项全国大奖。

examples.en: At first the town rejected the plan.
examples.cn: 起初镇上拒绝了该计划。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「福斯特」—— 福气最先到的人 → first 第一、首先

root: first 是古英语 fore「在前」的最高级 fyrest「最前」的延续，上溯日耳曼词根 fur-「向前」；核心是「队列与时间的最前端」。

sensesIntro.en: From position in a line outward to time, importance, instruction and the winning place.
sensesIntro.cn: 从队列位置扩展到时间、重要性、指令次序与夺冠之位。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the front of every line, visible before all else.
core.cn: 核心意象：一切队列的最前端，先于其他被看见。

branches.en: THE START: first in order and in time.
branches.cn: 起点：次序与时间上的最先。

branches.en: THE TOP: importance ranked first.
THE LIST: firstly, before the rest.
THE PODIUM: first place at the end.
THE MEMORY: first times are kept longest.

intro.en: The fore family lines up space and time: before, foremost, firstborn.
intro.cn: fore 词族为空间与时间排序：before、foremost、firstborn。

latinIntro.en: Latin used primus 'first', root of prime and primary, unrelated to the Germanic fore.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语用 primus「第一」（prime、primary 的词根），与日耳曼的 fore 无关。

items.meaning: the leader of a work crew
